0B603DDCB7BA4497AEF7D78826D4568E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D232A8054F53435797B06128597787C3.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

24B78C846C924E7282BBAC010A373836.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

0CF2EA1F853C405DA15EA2388706CE40.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Louisiana Student Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy

ED15AAE0DFE50131083468A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

ED155330DFE50131083368A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

ED1509C0DFE50131083268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

ED14BEA0DFE50131083168A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

ED1473E0DFE50131083068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

ED142840DFE50131082F68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

ED13D940DFE50131082E68A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

ED138530DFE50131082D68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

ED133CD0DFE50131082C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

ED129B10DFE50131082A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

ED124710DFE50131082968A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

ED11EF60DFE50131082868A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

ED1140D0DFE50131082668A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

ED10C780DFE50131082568A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

ED106EF0DFE50131082468A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

ED1020F0DFE50131082368A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.

ED0FC770DFE50131082268A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.

ED0F7260DFE50131082168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

ED0EE270DFE50131081F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

ED0E9930DFE50131081E68A86D17958E.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

ED0E4C00DFE50131081D68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

ED0DF510DFE50131081C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

ED0D9ED0DFE50131081B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

ED0CA490DFE50131081868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

ED0C5660DFE50131081768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

ED0C0490DFE50131081668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

ED0B6930DFE50131081468A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

ED0ACFD0DFE50131081268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

ED0A7DF0DFE50131081168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

ED09CEC0DFE50131080F68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

ED098650DFE50131080E68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

ED093F60DFE50131080D68A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

ED08F200DFE50131080C68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

ED083BA0DFE50131080A68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.

ED07E600DFE50131080968A86D17958E.description: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

ED078460DFE50131080868A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.

ED073820DFE50131080768A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.

ED06E6E0DFE50131080668A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

ED069A10DFE50131080568A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

ED064E40DFE50131080468A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

ED055970DFE50131080168A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

ED051150DFE50131080068A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

ED04CA90DFE5013107FF68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

ED043D50DFE5013107FD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

ED03F4E0DFE5013107FC68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

ED03A6D0DFE5013107FB68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

ED030100DFE5013107F968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

ED02B6F0DFE5013107F868A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

ED0224E0DFE5013107F668A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point[s]").

ED01D4B0DFE5013107F568A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or a drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., how characters interact]").

ED018310DFE5013107F468A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

ED0136F0DFE5013107F368A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.

ED00E210DFE5013107F268A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

ED0081B0DFE5013107F168A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

ED0006C0DFE5013107F068A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two pages in a single sitting.

ECFF8CB0DFE5013107EF68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

ECFF3D10DFE5013107EE68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

ECFEAAA0DFE5013107EC68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

ECFE6030DFE5013107EB68A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

ECFE1540DFE5013107EA68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

ECFDB5B0DFE5013107E968A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

ECFD6810DFE5013107E868A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

ECFD1D90DFE5013107E768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

ECFCD440DFE5013107E668A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

ECFC8620DFE5013107E568A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

ECFC3110DFE5013107E468A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).

ECFBD400DFE5013107E368A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

ECFB82B0DFE5013107E268A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

ECFB31A0DFE5013107E168A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

ECFAE9A0DFE5013107E068A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

ECFAA0E0DFE5013107DF68A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

ECFA5300DFE5013107DE68A86D17958E.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

ECF43D90DFE5013107DD68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

ECF3E540DFE5013107DC68A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

ECF2FAC0DFE5013107D968A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

ECF26E90DFE5013107D768A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

ECF227A0DFE5013107D668A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

ECF1E050DFE5013107D568A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

ECF19870DFE5013107D468A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

ECF14D90DFE5013107D368A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

ECF0F0E0DFE5013107D268A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

ECF09E50DFE5013107D168A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

ECF00DB0DFE5013107CF68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

ECEFC3C0DFE5013107CE68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

ECEF75F0DFE5013107CD68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

ECEEC980DFE5013107CB68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

ECEE6B50DFE5013107CA68A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

ECEE0D50DFE5013107C968A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

ECEDA970DFE5013107C868A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

ECED56B0DFE5013107C768A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

ECECC350DFE5013107C568A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

ECEC78E0DFE5013107C468A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

ECEB8320DFE5013107C168A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

ECEAAA20DFE5013107BE68A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

ECEA5CC0DFE5013107BD68A86D17958E.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

ECE6A9F0DFE5013107B268A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

ECE5C1E0DFE5013107AF68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.

ECE57660DFE5013107AE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

ECE4CEB0DFE5013107AC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.

ECE464D0DFE5013107AB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

ECE40FD0DFE5013107AA68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

ECE380C0DFE5013107A868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

ECE33560DFE5013107A768A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.

document.title: Louisiana Content Standards for English Language Arts

EB2538E0DFE50131044C68A86D17958E.description: Using inductive and deductive reasoning skills across oral, written, and visual texts

EB24DC50DFE50131044B68A86D17958E.description: Interpreting the effects of an author's purpose (reason for writing) and viewpoint (perspective)

EB246FB0DFE50131044A68A86D17958E.description: Using reasoning skills (e.g., categorizing, prioritizing), life experiences, accumulated knowledge, and relevant available information resources to solve problems in oral, written, and visual texts

EB243100DFE50131044968A86D17958E.description: Using comprehension strategies (e.g., summarizing, recognizing literary devices, paraphrasing) to analyze oral, written, and visual texts

EB23EF90DFE50131044868A86D17958E.description: Students apply reasoning and problem-solving skills to reading, writing, speaking, listening, viewing, and visually representing.
comments: Students use language daily to solve problems and deal with issues surrounding them. In order to respond effectively to these situations, students need to use the English Language Arts clearly, fluently, strategically, critically, technologically, and creatively. Students should use reasoning skills as they pose questions, plan, predict, investigate, hypothesize, speculate, and communicate about issues they encounter in academic subjects as well as in everyday life.

EB23B040DFE50131044768A86D17958E.description: Classifying and interpreting various genres according to their unique characteristics

EB237000DFE50131044668A86D17958E.description: Identifying, comparing and responding to a variety of classic and contemporary fiction and non-fiction literature from many genres (e.g., novels, drama)

EB232E30DFE50131044568A86D17958E.description: Comparing/contrasting and responding to United States and world literature that represents the experiences and traditions of diverse ethnic groups

EB22DF40DFE50131044468A86D17958E.description: Students read, analyze, and respond to literature as a record of life experiences.
comments: Literature is a record of life experiences as set forth in various writings (e.g., history, novels, poetry, science fiction, essays, news articles, logs). The study of literary texts recognizes characteristics of enduring literature, discovers and reviews the elements of various genres, identifies diverse perspectives, and distinguishes cultural traditions. The study of literature and writers of the United States and throughout the world gives students an appreciation of other cultures in a global society. Through a comprehensive literature program, students learn to make connections between literary texts and their own lives, to develop their own perspectives, and to analyze different viewpoints toward events, circumstances, and issues in our complex society.

EB229510DFE50131044368A86D17958E.description: Identifying and interpreting graphic organizers (e.g., flowcharts, timelines, tree diagrams)

EB2251C0DFE50131044268A86D17958E.description: Citing references using various formats (e.g., endnotes, annotated bibliographies)

EB220A40DFE50131044168A86D17958E.description: Using available technology to produce, revise, and publish a variety of works (e.g., documented research reports, investigative reports, annotated bibliographies)

EB21BC30DFE50131044068A86D17958E.description: Locating, gathering, and selecting information using formal outlining, paraphrasing, interviewing, and surveying to produce documented texts and graphics

EB212500DFE50131043E68A86D17958E.description: Identifying and using organizational features of printed text, other media, and electronic information (e.g., microprint, CD-ROM, e-mail)

EB20D3D0DFE50131043D68A86D17958E.description: Students locate, select, and synthesize information from a variety of texts, media, references, and technological source acquire and communicate knowledge.
comments: The information and technology age demands multifaceted approaches to accessing facts, images, and text from an array of information sources (e.g., libraries, electronic data, audio and video materials).The vast amount of available sources includes the reading and retrieval of information through the use of technology. The ability to identify topics, to gather information, and to evaluate, assemble, and interpret findings from an assortment of sources is one of the most essential real-life skills that students need in order to acquire and communicate knowledge in a rapidly changing world.

EB2096A0DFE50131043C68A86D17958E.description: Participating in a variety of roles in group discussions (e.g., facilitator, recorder)

EB2058C0DFE50131043B68A86D17958E.description: Listening and responding to a wide variety of media

EB2018E0DFE50131043A68A86D17958E.description: Speaking and listening for a variety of audiences (e.g., classroom, real-life, workplace) and purposes (e.g., awareness, concentration, enjoyment, information, problem solving)

EB1FD6B0DFE50131043968A86D17958E.description: Using the features of speaking (e.g., audience analysis, message construction, delivery, interpretation of feedback) when giving rehearsed and unrehearsed presentations

EB1F3370DFE50131043768A86D17958E.description: Speaking intelligibly, using standard English pronunciation and diction

comments: Communication is dependent on the interpersonal skills of speaking and listening and on the ability to work collaboratively with different people. Since information can be conveyed in various ways (e.g., between persons or groups, between persons and technological mechanisms, or between mechanisms), students need to understand the communication process: the concepts of sender and receiver, the ability to track communication breakdowns, recognition of verbal and nonverbal cues, and the art of follow-through. Understanding the communication process and applying this understanding to different audiences, purposes, and contexts will enable students to achieve effective communication in real-life situations.
EB1EC670DFE50131043668A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate competence in speaking and listening as tools for learning and communicating.

EB1E8240DFE50131043568A86D17958E.description: Spelling accurately using strategies and resources (e.g., glossary, dictionary, thesaurus, spell check) when necessary

EB1D3E30DFE50131043068A86D17958E.description: Students communicate using standard English grammar, usage, sentence structure, punctuation, capitalization, spelling, and handwriting.
comments: Communication is dependent on the practical application of standard English to real-life situations. Students need to be able to apply the knowledge of the systems and structures of standard English in order to develop, discuss, and critique various texts. When students connect the study of grammar and language patterns to written, spoken, and visual compositions, they begin to incorporate these skills into their own working knowledge and ensure that the texts that they create are well received and understood.

EB1B62F0DFE50131042968A86D17958E.description: Students write competently for a variety of purposes and audiences.
comments: Writing is a flexible, recursive process that requires an awareness of purpose and audience, an ability to draw on prior experience, and a knowledge of various approaches. To attain the necessary skills to create written text, students should engage in frequent, meaningful writing activities. As students use different strategies and modify their writing for various purposes and audiences, they become competent in communicating in real-life situations.

EB1A1AA0DFE50131042468A86D17958E.description: Using knowledge of word meaning and developing basic and technical vocabulary using various strategies (e.g., context clues, idioms, affixes, etymology, multiple-meaning words)

comments: As students move through the stages of reading development from emergent literacy to fluent, strategic reading, they learn to draw upon their prior experiences, their interactions with other readers and writers, their knowledge of word meaning and of other texts, their word identification strategies, and their understanding of textual features (e.g., semantic, syntactic, graphophonic). Students need to learn how to vary their approaches according to the type of text (e.g., written, spoken, or visual, including formal, informal, literary, and practical), their purpose in reading, and their own knowledge and experiences. Therefore, students should read for a variety of purposes and within a variety of contexts in order to become proficient and knowledgeable readers. Discovering various purposes and exploring and studying different kinds of texts will enable students to become lifelong readers and productive members of society and the workplace.

document.title: Louisiana Student Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy

EF230160DFE501310C3668A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

EF22A240DFE501310C3568A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

EF223E30DFE501310C3468A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole, paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

EF21ED20DFE501310C3368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

EF219ED0DFE501310C3268A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

EF214CB0DFE501310C3168A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

EF20F390DFE501310C3068A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

EF20A6F0DFE501310C2F68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

EF205920DFE501310C2E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 11—12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

EF1FB890DFE501310C2C68A86D17958E.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

EF1F6700DFE501310C2B68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EF1E1560DFE501310C2768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

EF1CFC60DFE501310C2468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

EF1B99A0DFE501310C2068A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

EF1B4930DFE501310C1F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

EF1AFD10DFE501310C1E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

EF1A61A0DFE501310C1C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EF197330DFE501310C1968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

EF18BDC0DFE501310C1768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

EF185F10DFE501310C1668A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

EF17FC00DFE501310C1568A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

EF17AE00DFE501310C1468A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed, and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

EF16E700DFE501310C1268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

EF168060DFE501310C1168A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

EF161DA0DFE501310C1068A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

EF15D1B0DFE501310C0F68A86D17958E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

EF1585E0DFE501310C0E68A86D17958E.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

EF153970DFE501310C0D68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

EF14EB90DFE501310C0C68A86D17958E.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 11—12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

EF13F1D0DFE501310C0968A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

EF139550DFE501310C0868A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

EF1330C0DFE501310C0768A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

EF1279B0DFE501310C0568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

EF1229C0DFE501310C0468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

EF11D880DFE501310C0368A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

EF10A0A0DFE501310C0068A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

EF1000F0DFE501310BFE68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

EF0FAE10DFE501310BFD68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the specific task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and over-reliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

EF0F5970DFE501310BFC68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

EF0E9230DFE501310BFA68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

EF0E3550DFE501310BF968A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

EF0DDF60DFE501310BF868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

EF0D40B0DFE501310BF668A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation provided (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

EF053B50DFE501310BDF68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

EF04EFD0DFE501310BDE68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

EF0451B0DFE501310BDC68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

EF040080DFE501310BDB68A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

EF03AC90DFE501310BDA68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

EF035AE0DFE501310BD968A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

EF030C10DFE501310BD868A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

EF02BCF0DFE501310BD768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

EF026720DFE501310BD668A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

EF0208D0DFE501310BD568A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

EF01AE60DFE501310BD468A86D17958E.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

EF015210DFE501310BD368A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

EF00FDD0DFE501310BD268A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

EF00A770DFE501310BD168A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

EF003EF0DFE501310BD068A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

EEFFCF10DFE501310BCF68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

EEFF78E0DFE501310BCE68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

EEFF1DC0DFE501310BCD68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

EEFEC460DFE501310BCC68A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

EEFE76C0DFE501310BCB68A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

EEFE2A30DFE501310BCA68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

EEFD3D30DFE501310BC768A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

EEFC89A0DFE501310BC568A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

EEFC3090DFE501310BC468A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

EEFBE000DFE501310BC368A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

EEFB8D10DFE501310BC268A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

EEFB2F30DFE501310BC168A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

EEFADB90DFE501310BC068A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

EEFA6B30DFE501310BBF68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

EEF9A670DFE501310BBD68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

EEF90840DFE501310BBB68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

EEF86840DFE501310BB968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

EEF81410DFE501310BB868A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

EEF79DF0DFE501310BB768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

EEF74070DFE501310BB668A86D17958E.description: Synthesize information from a range of sources (e.g., texts, experiments, simulations) into a coherent understanding of a process, phenomenon, or concept, resolving conflicting information when possible.

EEF6EC70DFE501310BB568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in a science or technical text, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

EEF69D30DFE501310BB468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., quantitative data, video, multimedia) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

EEF5EEF0DFE501310BB268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, identifying important issues that remain unresolved.

EEF5A030DFE501310BB168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the text structures information or ideas into categories or hierarchies, demonstrating understanding of the information or ideas.

EEF54DE0DFE501310BB068A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 11—12 texts and topics.

EEF48590DFE501310BAE68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks; analyze the specific results based on explanations in the text.

EEF42C60DFE501310BAD68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; summarize complex concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms.

EEF3DB40DFE501310BAC68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to important distinctions the author makes and to any gaps or inconsistencies in the account.

EEF344B0DFE501310BAA68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

EEF2F5F0DFE501310BA968A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

EEF2A270DFE501310BA868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

EEF24850DFE501310BA768A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

EEF1DB60DFE501310BA668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

EEF18AB0DFE501310BA568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

EEF0E6B0DFE501310BA368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

EEF08650DFE501310BA268A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

EEF02FF0DFE501310BA168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

EEEF7C20DFE501310B9F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

EEEF09F0DFE501310B9E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

EEEE8980DFE501310B9D68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

EEEDDEF0DFE501310B9B68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

EEED8FA0DFE501310B9A68A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

EEED2B40DFE501310B9968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

EEECDDF0DFE501310B9868A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

EEEC91D0DFE501310B9768A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

EEEC4400DFE501310B9668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

EEEBA310DFE501310B9468A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

EEEB4510DFE501310B9368A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

EEEAE3D0DFE501310B9268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

EEEA27E0DFE501310B9068A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

EEE9CF10DFE501310B8F68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

EEE97800DFE501310B8E68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

EEE87980DFE501310B8B68A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

EEE82A50DFE501310B8A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

EEE785B0DFE501310B8868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

EEE73690DFE501310B8768A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

EEE69260DFE501310B8568A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

EEE63750DFE501310B8468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

EEE5C730DFE501310B8368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

EEE50F70DFE501310B8168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

EEE4B6F0DFE501310B8068A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

EEE46460DFE501310B7F68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

EEE364C0DFE501310B7C68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

EEE315A0DFE501310B7B68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

EEE2C880DFE501310B7A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

EEE27630DFE501310B7968A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

EEE21AB0DFE501310B7868A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

EEE18310DFE501310B7668A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

EEE13330DFE501310B7568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

EEE0D2D0DFE501310B7468A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

EEE02580DFE501310B7268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

EEDFD3D0DFE501310B7168A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

EEDF82D0DFE501310B7068A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

EEDEC6F0DFE501310B6E68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

F2E06F70DFE50131136868A86D17958E.description: Show signs of excitement and willingly participate when exposed to new activities, skills, and movements.

F2E02610DFE50131136768A86D17958E.description: Displays a willingness to participate in new activities.

F2DFD680DFE50131136668A86D17958E.description: Identify a limited number of emotions related to how the student feels while participating in physical activity.

F2DF8A70DFE50131136568A86D17958E.description: Looks forward to participating in physical activity.

F2DF3C60DFE50131136468A86D17958E.description: Distinguishes feelings about and during physical activity.

F2DEE790DFE50131136368A86D17958E.description: Identify and demonstrate acceptable responses to challenges, successes, and failures during physical activity.

F2DEA030DFE50131136268A86D17958E.description: Describes the feelings that result from challenges, successes, and failures in physical activity, alone or in groups.

F2DE5130DFE50131136168A86D17958E.description: Understands that physical activity provides the opportunity for enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and social interaction.

F2DDF610DFE50131136068A86D17958E.description: Encourage fellow students who experience difficulty with a task by giving verbal cues, visual cues, or demonstrations.

F2DDAFB0DFE50131135F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates a willingness to help a fellow student who has difficulty completing a skill.

F2DD6FE0DFE50131135E68A86D17958E.description: Show appropriate sportsmanship and sensitivity to diversity and gender issues.

F2DD2F20DFE50131135D68A86D17958E.description: Interacts with others regardless of personal differences (e.g., gender, ethnicity, disability).

F2DCECB0DFE50131135C68A86D17958E.description: Positively interacts with others regardless of physical abilities.

F2DC9700DFE50131135B68A86D17958E.description: Recognizes the importance of seeking out, participating with, and showing respect for people of like and different physical abilities.

F2DC5320DFE50131135A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates an understanding and respect for differences among people in physical activity settings.

F2DC1300DFE50131135968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate socially acceptable conflict resolution during class activity.

F2DBD210DFE50131135868A86D17958E.description: Exhibit behavior which exemplifies responsibility to avoid conflict, best effort, cooperation, and compassion/empathy in a controlled setting.

F2DB9040DFE50131135768A86D17958E.description: Applies the elements of socially acceptable conflict resolution in physical activity settings (e.g., cooperation, sharing, consideration).

F2DB4C70DFE50131135668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate cooperation and consideration of others in group activities (sharing and taking turns).

F2DB03E0DFE50131135568A86D17958E.description: Works cooperatively (e.g., takes turns, is supportive, assists partner) with another to complete an assigned task.

F2DAAF80DFE50131135468A86D17958E.description: Engage in activity in a diverse group setting without interfering with others.

F2DA5DA0DFE50131135368A86D17958E.description: Acknowledges the importance of being aware of one's surroundings and acting in a safe manner in physical activity settings.

F2DA0E10DFE50131135268A86D17958E.description: Follow rules, directions, and procedures from the instructor with little reinforcement.

F2D9BD90DFE50131135168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates established protocols with little reinforcement (e.g., playground, classroom, and gymnasium).

F2D97A10DFE50131135068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings.

F2D92FB0DFE50131134F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and identify flexibility activities for shoulders, legs, and trunk.

F2D8DEA0DFE50131134E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates moving each joint through a full range of motion.

F2D898E0DFE50131134D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate sufficient muscular strength to bear body weight for climbing, hanging, and momentary body support of the hands.

F2D849F0DFE50131134C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to correctly perform a variety of teacher-led exercises for muscular strength and endurance (crunches, squats, lunges, push-up choices, dyna bands, musical activities).

F2D80140DFE50131134B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates activities that increase muscular strength and endurance.

F2D7BCF0DFE50131134A68A86D17958E.description: Identify that moderate levels of physical activity increase heart rate, respirations and perspiration, etc. (e.g., running, galloping, and hopping).

F2D76230DFE50131134968A86D17958E.description: Describe and participate in a variety of physical activities that promote positive gains in health-related fitness.

F2D72050DFE50131134868A86D17958E.description: Identifies physiological signs of moderate physical activity (e.g., fast heart rate, sweating, increased breathing).

F2D6DF50DFE50131134768A86D17958E.description: Identify changes in the body that occur during vigorous activity.

F2D69C30DFE50131134668A86D17958E.description: Participate in sustained moderate to vigorous physical activities that cause increased heart rate and respiration for a period of 15 minutes.

F2D655C0DFE50131134568A86D17958E.description: Sustains activity from moderate to vigorous intensity levels while participating in physical activity.

F2D60D90DFE50131134468A86D17958E.description: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of physical fitness.

F2D5C280DFE50131134368A86D17958E.description: Exhibit both verbal and non-verbal indicators of enjoyment of, or satisfaction with, physical activity.

F2D56850DFE50131134268A86D17958E.description: Willingly attempt new physical activities when presented with a variety of options.

F2D517C0DFE50131134168A86D17958E.description: Experiences and expresses satisfaction from participation in physical activity.

F2D4C940DFE50131134068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between active and inactive lifestyles.

F2D48280DFE50131133F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the location of the heart and lungs and explain what happens during physical exercise.

F2D43EB0DFE50131133E68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledges that physical activity is good for personal well-being.

F2D3F930DFE50131133D68A86D17958E.description: Participate regularly in a variety of physical activities outside of physical education class (e.g., playing, bicycling, sport teams, gymnastics, and/or dance). Record using teacher/parent log.

F2D3AC70DFE50131133C68A86D17958E.description: Participates regularly in vigorous activities outside of physical education class.

F2D328E0DFE50131133A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to combine any locomotor skills with concepts of space and direction.

F2D27FF0DFE50131133868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to follow directions given the following movement vocabulary: high/low, close/far, alone/partner, curved, zigzag, right/left, clockwise/counter/clockwise.

F2D1D230DFE50131133668A86D17958E.description: Apply movement concepts of walk, jog, and run to a variety of basic skills (e.g., throw, catch, strike)

F2D19000DFE50131133568A86D17958E.description: Identify major characteristics of the basic manipulative skills of throw (using underhand, sidearm, or overhand), catch, kick, and strike (using underhand, sidearm, or overhand).

F2D10860DFE50131133368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between a jog and a run, a hop and a jump, and a gallop and a slide.

F2CFBE40DFE50131132F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates and uses a variety of relationships with objects.

F2CF6EC0DFE50131132E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to incorporate language arts, math, social studies, and science concepts through movement activities (alphabetize letters, counting, mass and weight, folk/line dance).

F2CF2E40DFE50131132D68A86D17958E.description: Identify various body parts and levels in performing physical activities.

F2CEEAE0DFE50131132C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the right and left sides of the body and movement from right to left and left to right (dance).

F2CEA3A0DFE50131132B68A86D17958E.description: Integrates other content areas through movement.

F2CE5320DFE50131132A68A86D17958E.description: Applies movement concepts and principles to the learning and development of motor skills.

F2CD8ED0DFE50131132768A86D17958E.description: Create or imitate movement in response to rhythmic patterns and music.

F2CD47A0DFE50131132668A86D17958E.description: Performs basic rhythmic skills alone, with a partner, or within a group.

F2CC8DD0DFE50131132468A86D17958E.description: Strike an object upward continuously while using a variety of body parts and/or equipment.

F2CC4AC0DFE50131132368A86D17958E.description: Move to approach a stationary ball and kick it.
