C4C4BE7569CB40BA90115E4C03AB8CAB.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

25027B0B4BE24BE786499E722108CF41.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

83A52E061248476E9B457E70789F0576.description: Look for and make use of structure.

B0447C48A49F417BA91421FA5EDAFC13.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

EBC63FA2AEA443FA9376071F4409B189.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

8D6CB6C22B5D4D9580820188CAB4A26D.description: Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy based on properties. (Students will define a trapezoid as a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides.)

65785084041B4B25B661F1D2AD734375.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.

4DD0704ED4384EF58459DDD38975B842.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

1689700EED16470D87ABF5EFA6C24DEF.description: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

6A507DF0E9F14DD6BB32CE53D0427C9D.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number in the ordered pair indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number in the ordered pair indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

E5A653C2CF014BD4A198AE6A76BF84BD.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

CD33D0BD4E6E405EA8DD3FB2598CDE0F.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

7A28DCC378AD4C539FA83793E33EC897.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

12D97A6E712A45A9821B5093C784D059.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

7039617DB6FC4888A4399A4D18A13012.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.

433BC01A55C04659A4799DC85140087C.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

F13B96AF63224EA192E41FF790926453.description: A solid figure that can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

D73FCF641E3B409080CBDAA7CA69E938.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

2E9456D6B71B4BD48915E6EAFDFE0740.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

BA7B27465EF94D4FADF6329DABB6D3FC.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

F87F63A111304CD59409598028378510.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

DF742478DB22445D8956B2B9BD1855C9.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system, and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m; 9 ft to 108 in).

1F401AF3FAB84723ABA90701CDAA1BF2.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

5B8A172C7E0C4E17BB3ED962290E8390.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

A1FDAEA84DFF403FB7C888A1327E0D46.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.

574DFE25135F4D16A52E4DBAC0BA7980.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

0A3755CE2EF844CBAA494B53697E2521.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

AA1A4279A2BD47D0AA5E56D52565B67C.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

0965C0D142D64FB4B8697E19FB2F7F6E.description: Relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n × a)/(n × b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

B02CADCA50F541AEB12F02637DF73871.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.

DFC3FF476E6B48A8B6D09CC89C4A6842.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case).

EE842CDCDF1D404C8DD2AA45CEC86AA6.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

D6316A95DDEA4BE4873F43AE011E0D58.description: Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

19C87778A2BF4A8B9AFBF0001DDCCC22.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

26F6DBAEA2F84A5E8725A75E0F969020.description: Construct a model to develop understanding of the concept of multiplying two fractions and create a story context for the equation.

D8C347DCEE7443C3B2784E350F0D7B73.description: Interpret the product (m/n) × q as m parts of a partition of q into n equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations, m × q ÷ n.

0DDEE43FAFFC4FF98712BCFA070F14C8.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

5950831A1AF449D4BDFA025B60525484.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

5F5404A17E984A648EC0318882151221.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

7709963D9C854738BEAAEA7D55E8D528.description: Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and justify the reasonableness of answers.

C962440131D043079B78D9D5FDEECC1C.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

6018F8D4C15D405FB4EA3EDAEC38140C.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions.

B83BAF812B1B49E8A085ED4348F7B5E9.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

18D88D2855D249019D37BDA2ADB5A4F7.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

60B2DA4E6C7E46699DCE5150A9ABA36F.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; justify the reasoning used with a written explanation.

A877BC078E1846618AB3DA47B8DF9E5F.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, subtracting multiples of the divisor, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and/or explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, area models, or other strategies based on place value.

9BBC24EBAAD043819992AB013E35A450.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

E9A2363FFD304330A57892930EAFAA86.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

88AEE94228584A4891CAFCC010386BD1.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

AA10783EA3364B0CAEE6084EB2C8957F.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

774E1A2C5E4A433A837723821BF43FCF.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

2FFA07AA099B4D93A41833B5C61896E4.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

4391E41F90294E8D86E6FF0C88638937.description: Explain and apply patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10. Explain and apply patterns in the values of the digits in the product or the quotient, when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

2579FA2B1087471CB69ACE484A362DFB.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

9E32054BE39B4C8BBEE33433CB1D8CFC.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

7A400449DD1D449A811E33E60EA82DD6.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

2C7471CF2EA5497789AFA73040527F56.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with whole numbers, fractions, and decimals, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

C9EFD80076D5405FA319FCD2284730F9.description: Use parentheses or brackets in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

7D20BDEB652B4DBA88260D221DBB6951.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A330ADFC56BC4EFBADA46A70B33FBCD3.description: Look for and make use of structure.

859D3AC7C5CC4CD5B861D6B1BE8AB7E4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

301456EA13F74628BED429341CB1B31D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

81FB2544795545F2B184C3382C7A1224.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

B73216B69D10432F92D260960EFF71D3.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

B9732410974C4DA6BEE753EBF23C9622.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

13D67EA2BC96450B8E0362F11528DA34.description: Solve word problems involving pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters, and bills greater than one dollar, using the dollar and cent symbols appropriately.

3DC8A378F5D04C79BEAD020BB5749F39.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

282C3E2BCFEC45AC9603B0FEAE2E711F.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

DAE6075BC4D64D2E8A3D07B1373F13F6.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

F3AC5A9FDE464DF5839AE16BE090D315.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

9B73386F66EC42939A3E7D6CE42D08E5.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

420D8C96B0DE45E08A540F6B1E58B5F9.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

76274E684F504255A86A28D5547F33B9.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

1CCC373273C34E60A365769DB40B1EE6.description: A plane figure that can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

CF78E44656574538B64F377BF872C8E4.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

3CE965A901C840D6ABDD7D63ECD0D88F.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

7CE7D602540A475CA66D0A727AC83E70.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

4415F5304479498FAF17866BE17E8F22.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units—whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

46AD103D9CE24DC0AAEB000C07180127.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

AF00E1ABBF8F4888B60AD7E05C51F619.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

3D7E003E87034F9FB8302E179778AC94.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

49B01AFA9E974FD9862E811318B02758.description: Calculate elapsed time greater than 60 minutes to the nearest quarter and half hour on a number line diagram.

0025E032108E464E9907938957CE5171.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes, within 60 minutes, on an analog and digital clock.

30E36BCD3F0F463C882E61F9C4BA21D2.description: Understand time to the nearest minute.

E1AE619135EB43E794BCB2911B6B0A48.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

E1FB8D5D31B44828880B5797991574B0.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

C04763802E5A4F0A9A57B269CBC5C2ED.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

8CE9D9B6FD4D40289A15F58F226B77E8.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

2587AD2FAD3A4EE78032F262FD07286D.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

BBC0283528A346B89AEF1F692C544C30.description: Explain equivalence of fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

75F21BFAD8FE4E48A2A7CFA91705974B.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

C76206C160AA4224BB4803496D4D6F09.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

1A69CE1CD4D049C8BAF546EB1056311B.description: Understand a fraction with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 as a number on a number line diagram.

D2E569B823C843E2A78873F6A8C36776.description: Understand a fraction 1/b, with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8, as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

2FF478CCFE924DB98152DA219BEC9D70.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

1143F7367722404ABABA6493765D2F71.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

16FE31B498514F0B95947E0AEC8DF52C.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

34DEB0FDD7F141C19544E75C12B3E46B.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

4E4A6096006846A18C24381AC0E4279F.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

042E753FC31341E5A877F7F897380918.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

FF1A144F76F04F6AB79DD1E46A361917.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

81755C33D9CF43FE8791D9208B530CE3.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

3027F50ED3A245AEA02318D48DC49D1D.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

F6D306C3132545A58C6029C6B3EDD2AF.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

A81643986DB749B5A41F52005C841002.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

A921D4E5A38240C2824E07D19897F926.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.

8780DB7105F14D2B81F45974249E895C.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

3F2D0CCEBE9743B4871BAA6F3C71D5C0.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

A490EC29BCB747C4B3CC7ADBAF99CA89.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

1D4D55E2990145E5AE32D73EB181333F.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

8DC6359E07B04F6F88D72D372CE9855E.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.

0E2CCA7711F44B8581A98B34E841EF3C.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

774E5DCF70B5473F944FE97564FC96B1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3E69BDFBD20B448CA216B22341F26D08.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5C760296FA1D48C3BB56340891C9E579.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

9AB7D237622341C38E29577D848395A1.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

A91EBB78B805481B971B6603A307F784.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

0CFBA5803836476AABD9FF80CF07731B.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

79615E08433A4E80B0EF0A2CE1DF3C07.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

44481DE952E64D9A8F7A3F8A6E1B3A2B.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; categorize functions as linear or nonlinear when given equations, graphs, or tables.

186A133DCC144CBAAEFFE567B98B5065.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

16169C6F804D4C88B755D5B62994B5BD.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

782AE47BE9054C1DB22BD6AEFB3239FA.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

1F5433941CCC44B6BA847088EE99A3E4.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

FE3A9D945D724133A48AE422C8B4DBF8.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

840DFA392BC94773BEB985EC5F282FBE.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

1ED6633221AD4A72AD35D7C665775288.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

B3AF77AE3C734203B6DA7A4496B92EAD.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

AE42ADA89D3C4ED8B3F23655B41E9DAD.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

16E52474411D4B358DD8B4A92E698E46.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

388D154C832F49A88AAE686459DBA7E4.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

CCC2ED362BAC40DE9AFE971581308491.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

0D5678BC0BF44CC2AA1D9456B2F58939.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

AF9A72A8284D4431B452D816333E4CC8.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

C3A8C879F13A4FC1AB38CD7B2E9D0B13.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

98DFFDC0E08F4E67959DAE517BAD51F2.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

47D7B3FE8A36450FAEFA39CF828EBE35.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

247FEA00CA4C405F8EBE04AE417611CC.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

C390272513F44519B4B7EF9452034A47.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

FD202F1692C140ABB7FB30038199BA86.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

0D50A688D4FD44E0815C69B85CA425E8.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

8A2A1E261DFB4E109ADE935B484C4BE5.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

DF768059954447A8B32935BF68E90518.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers, show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

FC3207C70B6E46D6A58BBE18E427B327.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including ft, in; km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. (Conversions are limited to one-step conversions.)

Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

9983B45A46864D729A18853DF91DD65F.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b. (Denominators are limited to 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.)

4D895EE04ABA4949A533704CE7050B11.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

B417032DD5824DB5A9C857D39F65E8F8.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

A230038A6AAA4290A1A7C90BE30251CE.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

B0BDE6A9279A46F1A6CBD5A05FB83859.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 11–12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5974967FE80949C18C8F27D5582A8553.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

A94410D3D3C642DE91DFB44A8BC0215F.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

13BE5B9E61C64BA383A3DBBFB9F8E609.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F8B788D8F10B45C7A692928A5A65BFB5.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage, Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

B839A9936E994C8DB1BD4338B9F9A701.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested.

BA05A06B173D44E1BD53E5408B32B037.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

46F6D51B33484520B93E3007A15BD06F.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts, audiences, and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

010D98611C594F10BB59BEBDC1E505CA.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

2328C17790A64B87A6770BA45996DA0B.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, while respecting intellectual property; convey a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, address alternative or opposing perspectives, and use organization, development, substance, and style that are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

B8E3DBF5C77646C9BAE8B6C441BA2AE2.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

156B3CEE09E64045A66E3FA0A7AC5B3C.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

876FBC7B82154766B9C570EF31E2FAB7.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

D975B23772CB4184941CCB751955E43E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

F39B99F2273B4856A88D7FB3A8C5A05F.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

0E500F2B9E7046F3B70C0DE8FFE77296.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

3F6DD4978CB8428F80F7D02068E152E3.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher- led) with diverse partners on grades 11–12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

FF3B895FC23344B2BF26AB685BD2EA56.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

C3E4EAEAD9BC4B56A00B3FE4C2FFD421.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. and world texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy ").

EFB7D899C34A4E929704F8BF98491753.description: Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of foundational works of literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

95A80FD2146446438B093E48B1EB5CCC.description: Draw relevant evidence from grade-appropriate literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

F7F9208669B94D3CAA2293192E9537B6.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA, APA).

25D86DB4169F4EBDA85AC52069A7713D.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

9B48424AA41449619D141DEAF9571566.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

CCE864084C544BDB963B185D43F20997.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

DAE11390543D44ABAB1517E6704C8939.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

79A9E2C36E0A40FF9E899FA47EDF0AC6.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

020821AEAE9048919D07AB8EFE7C008B.description: Provide a conclusion (when appropriate to the genre) that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

39437725249843BBBDE849F9E2C711A5.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and figurative and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, mood, tone and/or characters.

58B3B27D72714665AD16EDC8793A693E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

5A2F4D16814442A999B8CE5FF5931D21.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, mood, tone, events, and/or characters.

1567B0D9D9BA447A82771563511EE7C6.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

FC31EB9CFFCE47B7A135229C65EEE8E2.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

DECF4B07E0B74173BD8EB0E2BA07652E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

49DF080B237A41A79659D22D67186AED.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

FD80318BF6764CFA86DA606F724A1C9A.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

11EA981F9E3B442FA56277885FB1C4E5.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

E40340B4574049A09AF2085D40F384C2.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

A6ED696E72FF46C5A8BE2FCAA2BA0032.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

A87130CDD16F4F018F215DB55B09D68F.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

05497D27997B43A2A2429E2C0BAFB3AC.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

42177270F4224EA8A7D6FF9ECA492949.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

4C5032C886DD4BCF917055A739D5C244.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

B4D8BD9965C74D9BAC7A52177F64F1FE.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

4D18A3BAA6B344FCA0BB6566DD026081.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

EC7B1398023D4E9485E41E93F64E969E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7686FDAA9E1A41B7A88363581AF912D4.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11– workplace/postsecondary text complexity independently and proficiently.

D24DA0C0526D43EBBCF89D43C51E6BBF.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11– workplace/postsecondary proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

83A69CB77B4548178E31CEB51577872D.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

943A9A688646444A9585D01C7AEEFD02.description: Analyze foundational U.S. and world documents of historical and literary significance for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

0297E5EA464B44FBA950857EAB715041.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

8DD66922B0904BB59891225E8CEBEA7D.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

6DB0D6F5BCFA4C76B884A330526E579C.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is considered particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the student interpretation of power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

A9820233A2D647939BE48E8EDA34FB14.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

57DF0A557AB04303BC04ABAC70A46843.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

A138FDBDB2EC4BB79598F6EE9297CFC6.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

9A0FFA46DC8A4653966AFB557229DBE6.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

F62AB411CE7B442A9EC5EFF9888B8DF9.description: Cite strong, thorough, and relevant textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

93D2D3B6E32844D28264FE0A0E040D4F.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11– workplace/postsecondary text complexity independently and proficiently.

72FA9C47DFE44DFDB24D0DC41656E0D6.description: By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11– workplace/postsecondary text complexity proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

B33610C3E3244381B76872F52F80FE64.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9BF100D61356468E97FDB2039CEAC2E5.description: Demonstrate knowledge of foundational works of U.S. and world literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes and topics.

CB1854B3049F4EDCB5DBBAA8308F6E5D.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text.

A7648673EC2349F0ADCF81CD6DE7FE46.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

6D9C121DC96E47DFB0F15B4C27EC8FCD.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

9E91F7CC1F3244E386DF6FAD956F81AF.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

47C4B506637F41FA94815AFB82C59835.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama, including how the author develops character and setting, builds the plot and subplots, creates themes, and develops mood/atmosphere.

FE7AEAFAF7E8459990FDEE3815EAFC9A.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

7CFA88B4F77B4D2ABC2C850B8767025F.description: Cite strong, thorough, and relevant textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

document.title: K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Mathematics

14E3DCF450D44D84A9D659C2F63C200E.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

9EB1803B6DF7494F823CE76529F06278.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the
data.

1322D18A0FEF487A9ECDF729B848E6A8.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

CD9217CC354F4FE794B07B835FC3B0BC.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

16268F597BB7400D8AB163F60BAFAD2D.description:
Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given
functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and quadratic models.

F61E3DB52A524D8E8B67DBCC1821A359.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

338C5BDFB22549119E40A47C6520D89B.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the
context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible
associations and trends in the data.

44EEAC8C674F447F9EA0F150777389AA.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

0FF94922CB6F4A8FA305BBD821549B6B.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects
of extreme data points (outliers).

45A21D447E36464FAA5E9BC0EC28CE87.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread
(interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

99665CA5508E4F6A8ADBA01EFF966EAC.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

63AA9078566B4C499F1F7C7DCDCA3CD6.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear, quadratic, or exponential function in terms of a context.

B9D8FFF5D90D4AB0814C9937C84BBEC7.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

96B62CA368124C88A5BB8E2C7BBAD516.description:
Observe, using graphs and tables, that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity
increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

40F6B0468A16440D9719AC68E276BED9.description:
Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a
description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

20BF6AAEA1344B78BBC966A922763BC1.description:
Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative
to another.

F2A5F185AA174D2D9EF2D45EFB822BBA.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

156DC64D97CA4B0DBF71609F98EC62F0.description:
Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions
grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

4516EC48D1834FBB80F97DD333025873.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

02470E70F5AA4BD4A4C2E2B6D840C156.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

103D9B2D5A9F4F47830D1E2E0ACB3F65.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both
positive and negative). Without technology, find the value of k given the graphs of linear and quadratic
functions. With technology, experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph that
include cases where f(x) is a linear, quadratic, piecewise linear (to include absolute value), or exponential
function.

31B2382BD6AC41F8A5F932694472376F.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

BEA498EC2B9A40D0BF47C4C37517BADC.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

652CAB68708B4C8F845BC27C90E818FD.description:
Write a linear, quadratic, or exponential function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
★

4D6C43404F264DECBF798D48FECBDB4A.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

53345D0F2D1049BE8605FAEA6424CCB6.description:
Compare properties of two functions (linear, quadratic, piecewise linear [to include absolute value] or
exponential) each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal
descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another,
determine which has the larger maximum.

C8E65E80F32E4DFC926ABB3B94504EB4.description:
Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values,
and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

336D501BE4464F7095254E845426CCC1.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different
properties of the function.

9F833F373E94465B95D046CD3F660969.description: Graph piecewise linear (to include absolute value) and exponential functions.

418547DE1CEC4168AAAF7A49EBAA65C4.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

D322C4BB0D3B4582BC9A48842444A612.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using
technology for more complicated cases. ★

5B88AC0E61B74368B9294F2772294957.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a linear, quadratic, piecewise linear (to include absolute
value), and exponential function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate
of change from a graph. ★

223A83A0022F48A3A1949923CB4FF553.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory,
then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function. ★

52B9F1D2EA8E4336BBA44B6FEDC1E0E0.description:
For linear, piecewise linear (to include absolute value), quadratic, and exponential functions that model a
relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and
sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include:
intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and
minimums; symmetries; and end behavior. ★

B2734BA641964A68939F7C234E45B159.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

08DD0D890BD7462EB0C8CA2387098F8C.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions whose domain is a subset of the integers. Relate arithmetic sequences to
linear functions and geometric sequences to exponential functions.

CC9AEC8600604038A9BF325E0A32B8F3.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function
notation in terms of a context.

D88BFD7496DB457FBFED14AC954D4EC7.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each
element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then
f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

2274CD4BB49A46A5BEF5C2EC73178FAD.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

5B94EC4E093B4F46A16EF53813F52E66.description:
Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a
strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection
of the corresponding half-planes.

A6705E37300E4EF8A0499F9A8F20F000.description:
Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are
the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the
functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are
linear, polynomial, rational, piecewise linear (to include absolute value), and exponential functions.
★

584EED9669DF4BE38A2C1427B6669AD5.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate
plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

FA5A1966D0E84DD29E7D4BEC11BD0C29.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

0C6230FE92AF40EFA9F42CBD62E3B159.description:
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear
equations in two variables.

E99B5391B42742F1A37F6FEC4B74D5E2.description:
Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation
and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

307965FAFD5048278DA557B63919B933.description:
Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x
2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the
quadratic formula, and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the
quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as "no real solution.”

F77409D474A349A0834DF1CDA25D23D8.description:
Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the
form (x – p)
2 = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

89C988BFB2D7482F84BE39BC856FD7DF.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

CAC109C2C4364C7196021BC4D927A624.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by
letters.

6EAB41E7F615455994061795769D60B6.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

E131D29CF7BA4A09AD333AC6D59A255D.description:
Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous
step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to
justify a solution method.

E9DE1D08CE1746F39C2CE0F0E069FC37.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

F7FC21EDD37D46528D246D78907ADEFD.description:
Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For
example, rearrange Ohm’s lawV = IR to highlight resistance R.

0C94B77151D54188845FFE950A355CA6.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and
interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities
describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

65B5A255561A4CD0A03F16BD0A97CBE5.description:
Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on
coordinate axes with labels and scales.

09720343CCE74B5A90241A17C272B327.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from
linear, quadratic, and exponential functions.

F5F04A12C0734006980E9B4A1D92FC62.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

628E4D0BD2C64072AACB0DD64F9A66E9.description:
Identify zeros of quadratic functions, and use the zeros to sketch a graph of the function defined by the
polynomial.

33B8CC15433C4066BD89B5CB98945AF7.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

51BA4984AB8D42BA88D0997A5807E08C.description:
Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the
operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

F024E73C378644B4B5EE94D308534CFC.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

52FAB8036B5745C68D0110E46631C87D.description:
Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it
defines.

Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example,

document.title: K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Mathematics

8D5702B1F62C44F4A696F0285BE03EA7.description:
Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences
between parameters are significant.

AEBF4BDF6E5140E3A4A65C79D5B9C86E.description:
Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through
the use of simulation models for random sampling.

A23FBEC785A64A04B0426D7005053C3C.description:
Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies;
explain how randomization relates to each.

E7B163FBD7994FD3953BB71D0D4D9271.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

F245FD725BC545FEB4CE66996A07D260.description:
Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using
simulation. For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails
in a row cause you to question the model?

03CC5577784A4C3B9BE7F0C8E46C1107.description:
Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random
sample from that population.

A255F8135ADC4B24957B9D5005F95512.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

003B011B16884919B24F787A292BC975.description:
Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given
functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize exponential models.

8896D24759F74B0E811BC4676F9CD914.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

198BC504EFFF4D2184C4E8DFE34C556C.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

FFBA0F91543048108144036C1609DF93.description:
Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population
percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators,
spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

AA02E3862BA5451FB1BDEE449CA7E3AD.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

6B8E5681E79347928620FD98C76DA0CB.description:
Prove the Pythagorean identity sin2
(θ) + cos2
(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ),
or tan(θ) and the quadrant.

2B12F39F3E474CD7B592778089489615.description:
Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and
midline.★

617DEE3762374E7196D89A70B76146E3.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

EA01D58DBA474DDA8CD3DCAAB076C4FC.description:
Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real
numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

DD79306D8AA145AEAD7DF271A7BF7DB2.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

3B078C6E625B4A509E660CCDED4535CF.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

6A03EBA51ED7426DBD6992658B5DA6A4.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear, quadratic, or exponential function in terms of a context.

20EA06EC43424A5D8B624BC68E91F78D.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

EEB60A0F4DA1410FBF22A260C0C07929.description:

ct = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the
base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

9E3A1A7E64E94BDD9ECFB41A79260FED.description:
Given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table),
construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, to solve multi-step
problems.

E8B99F13CE3042959FB8F221C87506ED.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems

C9014FBFAFB746D78C0E660ABA4FADFD.description:
Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for
the inverse. For example, f(x) =2x3 or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.

313803649F984772BA8DA96B630685F9.description:
Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both
positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation
of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and
algebraic expressions for them.

FF5C8CCDD2F648F2BAF161617D11626B.description: Build new functions from existing functions

7BC0135DAFA34705AE85033E042C8E0B.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model
situations, and translate between the two forms. ★

4CF861DB2AAD4A8A9180342640DB0D9D.description:
Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the
temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these
functions to the model.

CB1A9B34F1FE4220812282058783E333.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

557EB6F4D9534FF7BA54E4DC685CBEA4.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities. ★

9454D7551FAB4597946038A38F80F697.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

C16C4FA94DB54EB097D019E9A3E0F78A.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically
in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic
expression for another, determine which has the larger maximum.

70B404B8BE6D4238A228534A54C226DA.description:
Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For example, identify
percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)t
, y = (0.97)t
, y = (1.01)12t, y = (1.2)t/10, and classify them
as representing exponential growth or decay.

AD531667303149B38CA647AC4BA1D746.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different
properties of the function.

4F0AF1102AA04F35ABED15B303921DD2.description:
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric
functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

DC6CF4D367EE469A808DD39A6E7732CD.description:
Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end
behavior.

043C42146EEE421BB6016414905A120F.description:
Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value
functions.

FD20557FD717494F8B4C4CB60429C38C.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using
technology for more complicated cases. ★

A1A945CFF0B6477586AD9D94B5CDA12A.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a
specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. ★

B645572C485748048804554C8579F43A.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

CBE2FAD7530144BFB1EFDD09397B501D.description:
Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are
the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the
functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are
linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions. ★

1475CE94216F47E5AB8B67F65EE9CF52.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

F2BD610CB26C49DBBC4F44A55670F5B2.description:
Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and
graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x2 + y2 = 3.

579E2D79A724463DAD5969C776445043.description:
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), limited to systems of at most
three equations and three variables. With graphic solutions, systems are limited to two variables.

Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x
2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the
quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the
quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

A00A203FBC8044DCBC10DB225B4231CF.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

2ADC1BBE9BEC47D69CF51441810BC54C.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

32B19F2835D04458AEB4A95F50ED39FD.description:
Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous
solutions may arise.

A81D8AD235ED4650AE19C084428C028F.description:
Explain each step in solving an equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step,
starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a
solution method.

583B2BFB9A0B42AEA45EF28E2012611E.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

DD65F47D5DAA4B8C94174B8F7AD004E9.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising
from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

C372B91034D845E59D60B0D2B497023A.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

C7D3914DAF8E44679082ED8BD6C7FD64.description:
Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x),
b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long
division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough
graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x
– a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

7A28D2845C1345C38B17DBA8ADD87C51.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

305A3734B53B4DE39DD0F42D8D68CDBB.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

613BC3C1B419409ABFFBDD400BA74D7B.description:
Apply the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1) to solve problems.
For example, calculate mortgage payments. ★

expression 1.15t can be rewritten as (1.151/12)

interest rate if the annual rate is 15%

F8F0829BE6BF4A92AA94DB79A4000437.description:
Use the relation i

multiply complex numbers.

Know there is a complex number i such that i

real.

77E748F0C71248A29617C69D07BCE03C.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

33BA38391E7E49BE8E8EE13FF7BF05FD.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

0AF64A166DB54EEFA732DC412E3B3421.description:
Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of
integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. For
example, we define 5
1/3 to be the cube root of 5 because we want (51/3)
