3 must equal 5.

23F5C4C11DE049E6BC4D4D3FB6594D9B.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

document.title: 2022 K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Social Studies

2D586CC3582549E08854DEB4D3FA48A1.description: Analyze patterns of population distribution and migration from 1300 to 2010.

0B78749AF7874B2B951A08766DF4E67F.description:
Analyze how advancements in communication, technology, and trade have affected global interactions
from 1300 to 2010.

C2865134462C43D4A953F0423ED66B2F.description:
Explain the effectiveness of institutions designed to foster collaboration, compromise, and development
from the post-Napoleonic era to the present.

CD852FD3964842ACB3338EF3D92C0C23.description: Explain how regional interactions shaped the development of empires and states from 1300 to 2010.

7A2BEA9B299E4311B7D1D6A3D287831D.description:
Analyze the causes and effects of the movement of people, culture, religion, goods, diseases, and
technologies through established systems of connection.

2DA260EC29274837B47EC73C22743847.description:
Explain the relationship between the physical environment and culture on local, national, and global
scales.

51958891B43048EE89C6E70A6DAFC79B.description: Analyze the effect that humans have had on the environment in terms of resources, migration patterns, and global environmental issues.

7258308656FC48AC93CC357738F0828D.description:
Analyze the effects of natural resources on the development of the Louisiana economy within the
context of global interdependence.

E368290EB33A4ECFB6C1973292B70D68.description:
Analyze trends of increasing economic interdependence and interconnectedness in world history from
1300 to 2010.

7801C89089814557B8FF4D4DD19DCC09.description:
Explain the economic, demographic, social, and cultural consequences of coerced labor throughout the
world.

60D75BC5BA614E22B2AE503DBF533E71.description:
Describe the causes of trade, commerce, and industrialization and how they affected governments and
societies from 1300 to 2010.

73931790BC4F42F6913E1C610DD937B3.description:
Analyze the influence of fiscal policies such as taxation and tariffs, trade embargoes, and spending
policies on national economies.

EF06336B388E402B92660689E596C174.description: Describe how global, national, and regional economic policies affect individual life decisions over time.

CB5E0C2A45D2499BAB2043595DE6DBBC.description:
Analyze goals, strategies, and effects of movements, both violent and non-violent, to gain freedom and
political and social equality in world history from 1914 to 2010.

5465D0C7CCAA44779477F6D1AAFF2CD1.description:
Analyze ideals and principles that contributed to the rise of independence movements from 1300 to
2010.

F34F57F2422947FE8FD8944169C976BC.description:
Analyze the roles of various countries during the Cold War and their roles in post-Cold War international
agreements and organizations.

D6AB3E267DC94E379D463435FE3FD443.description:
Analyze the causes of decolonization, methods of gaining independence, and geopolitical impacts of new
nation-states from 1945 to 2010.

DE286B2861E34EE8A24A2B7DC8EB2BD2.description:
Analyze the origins, consequences, and legacies of genocides that occurred in world history from 1914 to
2010.

0CFA4FC5EFDE4902A4CD918145F33E4B.description:
Describe various systems, laws, and policies of governance across world history in the period from 1300
to 2010 and their methods of maintaining power, including absolutism, communism, democracy, imperialism,
fascism, theocracies, monarchism, and republicanism.

BF413E27478143CDBB87DA3C118DC0D0.description:
Explain the powers and responsibilities of local, state, tribal, national, and international civic and
political institutions and their efforts to address social and political problems.

73D028C78EFF44BFAAD8C1C2D9AF7338.description:
Analyze the historical connections between Civil Law, the Napoleonic Code, and Louisiana’s system of
laws.

150CE4B64CE2475BB398AA0C0F93F4B3.description:
Compare and contrast systems of governance, including absolutism, communism, democracy,
imperialism, fascism, monarchism, and republicanism across world history in the period from 1300 to
2010 and their methods of maintaining power.

DDD7EEC070EE45C09D70EF2C869C630C.description:
Analyze how civic ideals such as freedom, liberty, and equal justice have influenced world governments
from 1300 to 2010.

AE893DEE55744109BAD0E069506D8D26.description:
Analyze the development and contribution of enlightenment ideas such as humanism, state of nature,
and natural rights to the structure and function of civic and political institutions from 1600 to 2010.

F90B9C21133D4EF689004395BDCDA96C.description:
Analyze how various religious philosophies have influenced government institutions and policies from
1300 to 2010.

808BF947C44D4F2DA7BAC28C0F40C472.description: Analyze the development of political and social structures throughout the world from 1300 to 1600.

52EAA05F53424EDEBBAF3C4ACCC16591.description: Analyze causes and effects of political revolutions of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries throughout the world.

94EE7FA84EF943749C9207EC2B1BD1B6.description:
Analyze the causes, effects, and reactions to imperialism from 1450 to 1945 and the experiences of
those who were colonized.

B075FF9D787A4A6291D0B59867A2546C.description: Analyze the causes and effects of global and regional conflicts in the world from 1300 to 2010.

D5544EB0BF3549CFBE0CFEF698A71163.description:
Analyze the origins and emergence of economic principles such as feudalism, mercantilism, capitalism,
socialism, and communism and their effects on political institutions throughout the world from 1300 to 2010.

BD81872D439842BC959607F3A6B97F48.description:
Analyze the relationship between events and developments in Louisiana history and world history from
1300 to 2010.

0B01C0BEE12F4B219BEBD8A8D084848B.description:
Analyze causes and effects of events and developments in world history from 1300 to 2010, including
fourteenth-century trade networks of Africa and Eurasia, Renaissance and Enlightenment in Europe, political
revolutions, industrialization, imperialism, global conflicts of the twentieth century, decolonization, and
globalization.

EA0945D0602740B7A506FE25F0821EF6.description:
Evaluate the influence of science, technology, innovations, and explain how these developments have
altered societies in the world from 1300 to 2010.

899B97E44DC64FE59F61610354DED0AC.description: Compare and contrast content and viewpoints.

88498F0B927841CC88217A179EF95971.description: Demonstrate an understanding of social studies content.

83A8A49CCE5847CE8D8CAA0282EED3FD.description:
Construct and express claims that are supported with relevant evidence from primary and/or secondary
sources, social studies content knowledge, and clear reasoning and explanations to:

09BC9C5BA5A1491CA290858B79211C49.description: Explain how the availability of sources affects historical interpretations.

3115203FC5064551A6EC82985942DC07.description: Compare and contrast multiple sources and accounts.

998DCCAFDF4949178125774B78798163.description: Use a variety of primary and secondary sources to:

716833FF9A2A4D5AA4D0DFB59C09290E.description:
Use geographic representations and demographic data to analyze environmental, cultural, economic and
political characteristics and changes.

E9E2D598CA854FCA95C45C88EDF832A3.description:
Analyze connections between events and developments in world history within their global context from
1300 to 2010.

4BDA7C9B59E5404D94641FB8B7797B48.description:
Analyze ideas and events in world history from 1300 to 2010 and how they progressed, changed, or
remained the same over time.

document.title: 2022 K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Social Studies

870C2310818D404285D4F73ECDC10B8C.description:
Explain important issues of the 2008 presidential election and the significance of the election of Barack
Obama.

74817EEA001D4823BDC4FEAA303B5205.description:
Analyze the presidential administrations of George H.W. Bush (Gulf War), Bill Clinton (influence of the
Contract with America on the legislative agenda, involvement in Bosnia), and George W. Bush
(September 11th).

C05292F6878247D488C1494268355CC0.description:
Compare the judicial philosophies of Supreme Court justices of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries,
including those of Antonin Scalia and Ruth Bader Ginsberg.

3B185964834C442FB86149CAD2CDF41F.description:
Explain events leading up to the September 11th attacks, the attack on New York City, the attack on the
Pentagon, Flight 93, President George W. Bush’s speech from Barksdale Air Force Base, the lives lost,
national unity in the aftermath, subsequent military operations, and the expansion of intelligence
agencies.

DB23AC41B3154285A6EA5F90CF26EDD0.description:
Analyze the effects of advancements in technology and media during the mid- to late twentieth century,
including the radio, television, and the internet.

D10604A3CFC945ED9EC261070E0FB11F.description:
Explain the causes and effects of domestic incidents, terrorism, and mass shootings, including the Ruby
Ridge incident, Waco siege, Oklahoma City Bombing, and Columbine High School shooting.

EB10EC28937F4F75B8BAD829D8225EC6.description: Explain causes of the Gulf War, its major military leaders, and unity on the home-front.

07B670ECA3644C178E9B14B81B416B68.description:
Explain the effects of major issues and events of the late twentieth century, including the HIV/AIDS
epidemic and disease perceptions, the war on drugs, and the space shuttle Challenger disaster.

BF921F63EAD4441695C6D78887A5833A.description:
Analyze Ronald Reagan’s political career (“A Time for Choosing” speech) and key policies of his
presidency (four pillars of Reaganomics reduce taxes, reduce federal spending, reduce government
regulation, tighten the money supply).

4E75A2EF42474DE089DDBD8E4EBBF0BA.description: Explain major U.S. events and developments in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries.

F265EBDDEED649C2AECD43B41303215E.description:
Explain how the failure of the communist economic and political policy, American foreign policy
pressure, and the assertion of American principles such as rights, equality, and liberty, led to the end of
the Cold War.

40E7B745A0104624B1841CE25678E359.description:
Explain factors that led to the end of the Cold War, the fall of communism, and the collapse of the Soviet
Union, including foreign policy pressures; Reagan’s “Tear Down this Wall” speech, the fall of the Berlin
Wall; glasnost and perestroika, and the decline of communism.

2815691920D04668B4C07004B199ACEC.description:
Explain the outcome and consequences of key Supreme Court decisions in the late twentieth century,
including Gideon v. Wainwright (1963), Miranda v. Arizona (1966), and Roe v. Wade (1973).

C27636E2D03C44A78A47747179757F55.description:
Explain the term "silent majority" in the context of Richard Nixon's presidency, the Watergate scandal,
his efforts to open trade with China, and his resignation.

13B89D3340AF4B2DB2E89DA26BAFEAEF.description: Analyze the role of Lyndon B. Johnson in the civil rights movement and the Vietnam War.

DD69B3C236FE47DC9E34A84BBC7F1657.description:
Analyze the effects of the campaign, election, inaugural address, presidency, and assassination of John
F. Kennedy.

CEA162338AAA4557AE0840B8159740B8.description: Explain the role of technology in the Cold War, including the Space Race, Sputnik, and Apollo 13 mission.

277E8428F78D473C90A33099FA1A5318.description:
Analyze the causes, course of, and consequences of the Cold War and its related crises and conflicts,
including the Berlin Blockade and Airlift, Chinese Civil War, Korean War, Suez Crisis, U-2 Incident, Cuban
Missile Crisis, Bay of Pigs Invasion, Vietnam War, Soviet-Afghan War, and Miracle on Ice.

6180A3C6F6BF4AA489F7CAF73EBBB4DB.description:
Describe the role of and major events and developments associated with key leaders during the Cold
War, including U.S. presidents (Harry. S. Truman, Dwight D. Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy, Lyndon B.
Johnson, Richard Nixon, Gerald Ford, Jimmy Carter, and Ronald Reagan); and soviet leaders (Nikita
Khrushchev and Mikhail Gorbachev).

3752C169BC484BC6B20951846AEE8760.description:
Compare ideas of the United States and Soviet Union during the Cold War, including the strengths of
American principles such as rights, equality of opportunity, liberty and equal protection under the law.

853DE733C8C04D2DB0FAB1E8F80D861C.description:
Analyze domestic policies of Dwight D. Eisenhower’s presidential administration including the Federal
Aid Highway Act of 1956.

5561DA442A4F43F08DB6D45672FE7950.description: Explain the causes and effects of the Marshall Plan and the formation of NATO and the Warsaw Pact.

26D8AFA153FC406494409F7F6388D39B.description:
Explain major events and developments of the post-World War II era in the United States and its
continued rise as a world power.

790E9069136F42A1953689A1F850EAE4.description:
Analyze the goals and course of the women’s rights movement of the mid- to late twentieth century,
with attention to House Resolution 5056, Equal Pay Act, Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education
Amendments, Equal Rights Amendment, and the advancement of women in government and various
professions.

8B9F901E4E3A47A780BE3DABE86F1086.description:
Analyze the goals and outcomes of the American Indian Movement (AIM) and the changing relationship
between Native Americans and the federal government, including before and after the Indian SelfDetermination and Education Assistance Act.

36042038C51B47B2A52FF8D3679BA094.description:
Analyze the role of the federal government in advancing civil rights, including Brown v. Board of
Education (1954), the Twenty-Fourth Amendment, the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and the Voting Rights Act
of 1965.

961C92EAA49C48679B806131C831ED08.description:
Analyze the role and importance of key events during the civil rights movement, including the murder of
Emmett Till, Baton Rouge Bus Boycott, Montgomery Bus Boycott, Little Rock Central High School
desegregation, Greensboro Sit-Ins, Freedom Rides, demonstrations in Birmingham, 1963 March on
Washington, Freedom Summer, and Selma to Montgomery Marches.

C1114973A3474DC89A1BD973821FD42B.description:
Explain how key individuals and groups contributed to the expansion of civil rights in the United States,
including A. Philip Randolph, Jackie Robinson, Rosa Parks, Medgar Evers, Ruby Bridges, Shirley Chisholm,
John Lewis, Malcolm X, and Thurgood Marshall.

9BAC6238EE9C4978B61C44E0F2D1E97C.description:
Analyze how the ideas, work, and life of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. influenced civil rights movements in
the United States, including civil disobedience, service with the Southern Christian Leadership
Conference (SCLC), writings such as his “Letter from a Birmingham Jail” and “I Have a Dream” speech,
and his assassination.

82CDB75E49614A76B9567ED3FDAFE67F.description:
Analyze the origins and goals of the civil rights movement, the effects of segregation (de jure and de
facto), and efforts to desegregate schools, transportation, and public places.

E8FF8AAAB9004ADDB8D17481D03B6E15.description: Analyze causes, major events, and key leaders of the civil rights movement.

8FA1BF0C70DA4D8983E1C4A6C31EE571.description: Describe the establishment of the United Nations, and its role in global affairs after World War II.

D4A9EF0451D34852853F7793105BA926.description:
Analyze the Holocaust, including the suspension of basic civil rights by the Third Reich, concentration
camp system, antisemitism, persecution of Jews and non-Jews, Jewish and non-Jewish resistance, the
role played by the United States in liberating Nazi concentration camps, immigration of Holocaust
survivors, and the Nuremberg trials.

8CC20DBEAD4C4B55B2AB73293B341882.description:
Explain the use of violence and mass murder as demonstrated by the Nanjing Massacre, the Holodomor,
the Holocaust, and the Bataan Death March and the treatment of U.S. prisoners of war.

A3D5195D574C4C1DBC6CACFBB33A25E4.description: Analyze the decision for and effects of dropping atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

303DBC94527344BD89811F19FC0E07CA.description:
Describe the roles of Franklin D. Roosevelt, Harry Truman, and the United States’ critical role in the
Allied victory.

1D103A6759494182879E933C7C7C6E12.description:
Explain the role of military intelligence, technology, and strategy during World War II including
cryptology, the Manhattan Project, island hopping and describe major battles of Midway, Normandy,
Iwo Jima, Okinawa, and Battle of the Bulge.

47B9A5C69E1743CEBF6D9C37AB8C4CBE.description:
Explain how the U.S. government managed the war effort on the home front, including campaigns to
conserve food and fuel, sale of war bonds, and coordination of wartime production.

1F4F06D8475D4847A44FC5085F64C537.description:
Explain the causes and effects of the internment of Japanese Americans in the United States during
World War II, as well as the decision in Korematsu v. United States (1944) and The Civil Liberties Act of
1988.

CB87A91ABBDF433181045C459FA31584.description:
Describe the sacrifices and contributions of American service members in the war effort including the
Tuskegee Airmen, Military Intelligence Service, 442nd Regimental Combat team, the 101st Airborne,
Women's Army Corps (WAC), Navajo Code Talkers, and the Army Signal Corps.

CAAE2B9C3FDB4163AD9FCD6AA4D1523A.description: Explain why Japan attacked Pearl Harbor and the response of the United States.

903582D8BE814F21823B642B60F86A08.description:
Explain efforts made by the U.S. government to prepare for war prior to entry including Cash and Carry
and Lend Lease policies, military maneuvers at Barksdale Air Force Base, and the Louisiana Maneuvers in
September 1941.

52456468BB3742F082BF9C36D7CEF397.description:
Explain the similarities and differences between totalitarianism and militarism in Imperial Japan,
communism in the Soviet Union, fascism in Mussolini’s Italy and Nazi Germany, and identify the major
powers of the Allies and the Axis powers.

6C95FF70B75847EC981488EADBFEBA4D.description: Explain the causes, course, and consequences of World War II.

B843FB788F6044D089AF322C545EFD5B.description:
Compare and contrast economic beliefs of Adam Smith, Karl Marx, John Maynard Keynes, and Milton
Friedman and analyze their influence on the economy of the United States.

D7AF8B47380743EF9217D73B8779D7FE.description:
Analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the New Deal in managing problems of the Great Depression
through relief, recovery, and reform programs, including the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), Works
Progress Administration (WPA), the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), and the Social Security Act (SSA).

C76BC395AD764EB380452AD4E27CFAE2.description:
Describe the causes and effects of the Dust Bowl, including natural disasters and unwise agricultural
practices, and how it exacerbated the Great Depression.

4C27C85CD47447E187F7BC06E019CA27.description:
Analyze the government response to the Great Depression, including actions taken by the Federal
Reserve, Congress, and the administrations of Herbert Hoover and Franklin D. Roosevelt.

030867BA056448C7AD2AEEBF8DF52956.description: Describe the effects of the Great Depression.

FF2F7D23EF0A4C77A02A4D3E1EC17DCD.description:
Explain the causes of the Great Depression, with an emphasis on how bank failures, buying stock on
margin, overextension of credit, overproduction, high tariffs and protectionism, and the 1929 stock
market crash contributed to the economic crisis.

0F15F143A88C4D3CB3A8E32A3CC8FE19.description: Describe the effects of the Great Depression and New Deal policies on the United States.

6A0985A4A0F84A39AA801DD48E186D94.description:
Describe the effects of racial and ethnic tensions, including the Chicago riot of 1919, Tulsa Massacre,
and re-emergence of the Ku Klux Klan.

72AAA5B99AA64A4E89B1254CA240494E.description:
Describe Prohibition in the United States and its consequences, including the development of organized
crime.

230BA007E75D4A6899B048802C992C46.description:
Analyze the effects of changes in immigration to the United States and migration within the United
States as a result of the Immigration Act of 1924 and the Great Migration.

357C5444BBA746E297F2EFBFE99FF577.description:
Analyze the rise in labor unions in the late nineteenth century and early twentieth century including the
American Federation of Labor-Congress of Industrial, the Organizations (AFL-CIO), the Industrial Workers
of the World (IWW), and the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters.

BB460A8AA4CF48978413BA760EF80EE1.description:
Analyze the causes and events of the First Red Scare including the Bolshevik Revolution, anarchist
bombings, the Immigration Act of 1918, and the Palmer Raids.

CADFE5C01E76454FA6256E2875FB6CEB.description:
Analyze how life in the United States changed as a result of technological advancements, including
automobile, airplane, and radio.

8FE16058537141849C132D9A0E2FEFD9.description: Describe changes in the social and economic status of women.

485ED79840DA415FA162932E2F586288.description: Explain the origins, main ideas, contributors, and effects of the Harlem Renaissance.

1D066C90AEF5492594C236114F193BF8.description:
Analyze the political, social, cultural and economic effects of events and developments after World War I
and during the 1920s.

F8BBA1FF8026447E922D091C4EAC3F11.description: Compare and contrast Wilson’s Fourteen Points and the Treaty of Versailles.

94664E6BB99C40AA9F2CF9DAE9DCB4FE.description: Explain why the Allied Powers won World War I.

20FC48E840014EF38323E5F2C901C34B.description: Analyze the suppression of dissent during World War I.

5BCF2DA7C06B471CA26F2F87AB55245C.description:
Describe the effects of major military events, the role of key people, and the experiences of service
members.

79294D7C77014440A4FC87E9571BE488.description: Explain the events leading to and reasons for U.S. involvement in World War I.

6F63CBF009E74E24821ED2407789F959.description: Describe the causes of World War I.

451CB61D39CC4CB8ACD88A9FB177B001.description: Analyze the causes, course, and consequences of World War I.

460C780FC21A4C96BAC47F7FF16A1352.description: Analyze ways in which the Suffrage Movement led to passage of the Nineteenth Amendment.

CEB19F7BB14C44FBACB3D965F2F4EBDE.description:
Analyze the life of Susan B. Anthony, including her time teaching, work for abolition, work for
temperance, and work for suffrage.

7583475BA1994BAB96CD23CCD1720B6D.description: Explain Elizabeth Cady Stanton’s reasons for writing the Declaration of Sentiments.

4BC21AE6D37C4421B98C0049FA5356E4.description: Compare and contrast the philosophies of Booker T. Washington, W. E. B. DuBois, and Marcus Garvey.

5EF809D83A2E4606B0400ADCA0D10956.description:
Explain the origins and development of Louisiana public colleges and universities, including land grant
institutions, Historically Black Colleges and Universities, and regional universities.

D1FA99F2C78641DE9CAFB7FEEF4D72FD.description:
Analyze the life of Booker T. Washington, including his enslavement and emancipation, the Tuskegee
Institute, and his Atlanta Exposition Speech.

CACF986CCFAA434AAE63847ABE7DCFFE.description:
Describe engagements between the U.S. government forces and Native Americans in the West following
the Civil War, including the Battle of Little Bighorn and Wounded Knee, and the effects of the Dawes Act
on Native Americans.

EDFE3C9620FF4A04A79C025AB892459D.description:
Analyze the life of Theodore Roosevelt, including his life in the West, the Rough Riders, his “Big Stick”
diplomacy, presidency, and conservation efforts.

13D04BFA51B746EB953AD295501D2D6A.description:
Analyze the Monroe Doctrine, the Roosevelt Corollary, and the development of U.S. foreign policy in the
late nineteenth century and early twentieth century including the Spanish-American War, the
acquisition of Hawaii and Alaska, construction of the Panama Canal, and the U.S. expedition to capture
Pancho Villa.

B1EFB5AEF0C94433B28C4A44275D6F4B.description:
Analyze the challenges that accompanied industrialization, including pollution, poor working conditions,
child labor, and food safety, as well as proposed solutions of the Progressive Era.

56376E5D123D4B569A929442E0CA31E2.description:
Explain push and pull factors for immigration to the United States in the late nineteenth and early
twentieth century and analyze the immigrant experience, including assimilation, challenges, and
contributions.

A3A6087CF9E44A329BC41D337890A0C8.description:
Explain the economic principles and practices that corresponded with America’s industrial and economic
growth after the Civil War including free markets, capitalism, mass production, division of labor, and
monopolies.

8F02CB37B3B344628EEF2678EF192D34.description: Describe how the physical geography of the United States affected industrial growth and trade.

AB48CE583684400ABB547AFFA9066FF7.description:
Describe the economic and social development of the United States in the late nineteenth and early
twentieth century and its emergence as a major world power.

44EC97B309FD4BE0992034C0E562AB33.description:
Explain the social, political and economic changes that resulted from Reconstruction including Jim Crow
laws, the role of carpetbaggers, scalawags, Radical Republicans, the Freedmen’s Bureau, sharecropping,
the creation of Black Codes, and the emergence of the Ku Klux Klan and the rise of violence and
intimidation of Black Americans.

AA88FB80AB0A451BAFFFA23EFAAD204F.description:
Compare and contrast resources of the Union and Confederate States and reasons attributed to the
Union winning the Civil War.

33E726CBFE024D16A55A5757BBE75664.description:
Analyze major battles of the Civil War, including Shiloh, Antietam, Gettysburg, Vicksburg, and the
capture of New Orleans.

582CAD58619041B8860016FDCC39587B.description:
Explain major and minor causes of the Civil War, especially the political tension surrounding the spread
of slavery.

3C6FAC1B8F3F484AB2E7323EBFFBD30A.description:
Analyze the life of Abraham Lincoln including his debates with Stephen Douglas, the meaning of his
“House Divided” speech, presidency and views on the Union, first and second inaugural addresses, the Emancipation Proclamation, the Gettysburg Address, particularly the origin and meaning of “last full
measure of devotion,” and his assassination.

67CFE83FEA6649B09F3ABA086B9DF5B5.description: Analyze the causes, course, and consequences of the Civil War and Reconstruction.

AC525F3F82F74674928567327B7287BD.description:
Evaluate the significance and extension of citizenship rights to Black Americans included in the
Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments to the Constitution of the United States.

F48282A5174D430C9BDBA6AEB6CE569B.description: Describe the purpose of the Emancipation Proclamation and its effects.

D6EFC36B2B7B45CEBC260129F5AF7930.description: Explain the outcome of the Dred Scott v. Sandford (1857) decision, including it later being called a “selfinflicted wound.”

780786709DDE4AA8A7C61D447F96622E.description:
Analyze the causes and effects of the Missouri Compromise, the Compromise of 1850, and the Kansas
Nebraska-Act.

4FF2BD7031DA44A6B1DFBC0C305D8C3A.description: Explain how slavery is the antithesis of freedom.

470A4022443D4B95975CA779E5014891.description:
Explain the effects of abolition efforts by key individuals including Sojourner Truth, William Lloyd
Garrison, Frederick Douglass, and Harriet Beecher Stowe.

8B5B6F1271AD4E6685BE1C63493080D6.description: Explain how slavery contributed to U.S. industrial and economic growth.

1E57FD02CB21434C9D93E55F750AF3FC.description: Describe the significance of invention of the cotton gin and its effects on slavery and economy.

08A4C669EE2A4BE39184D32B12B545CC.description:
Describe the experiences of enslaved people on the Middle Passage, at slave auctions, and on
plantations.

8A0E410A0F07403ABBA25AC0D268972B.description:
Describe the origins of the transatlantic slave trade, Middle passage, and early spread of slavery in the
Americas.

9E76E1550EB54B22BF12728FCF57631B.description: Analyze the development and abolition of slavery in the United States.

6649D558CF254310803DEAC38BF8E6EC.description: Explain the concept of Manifest Destiny and evaluate its effect on Westward Expansion.

A4C436080A104571AD2F180C33A8AD7E.description: Analyze the causes and effects of the Mexican-American War.

4D3180ADD99743078F0B3372A1C920D6.description:
Analyze the causes and effects of the Indian Removal Act and describe the role of key people involved in
Indian removal and the Trail of Tears including Andrew Jackson and John Ross.

0E41951D74CD4DFC90C204B9E54333DC.description: Explain the Louisiana Purchase and evaluate its effects on the United States.

546C78158E114618BA9239B70FD1C17F.description: Analyze key events associated with Westward Expansion during the early to mid-1800s.

1849A91867844EA5AF7EF61F72E54A4A.description: Explain and evaluate the concept of American exceptionalism.

D43D6601963241BEA6B0DB96317E4361.description:
Analyze how Alexis de Tocqueville’s five values are crucial to America’s success as a constitutional
republic (liberty, egalitarianism, individualism, populism, laissez-faire).

BCD5485A9B6344C9A38DE8710AE6DDD4.description:
Analyze major events and developments of U.S. presidents of the late 1700s to the early 1800s,
including the presidencies of George Washington (foreign and domestic policies, Farewell Address), John
Adams (Alien and Sedition Act), Thomas Jefferson (role in the Louisiana Purchase), and Andrew Jackson
(Bank War).

488B81A6AD134059BDF14EACD189B728.description:
Evaluate how the U.S. Constitution and Bill of Rights seek to prevent tyranny and protect individual
liberty and freedom, including through representation, limited government, separation of powers, and
checks and balances.

1DFD0FBE75934032BA5A407EE29E3932.description: Analyze the purposes of the Preamble of the Constitution.

324BCBADD63E461CB42F946ACD965B03.description: Explain the inadequacies of the Articles of Confederation.

3F77DB8E4FD642CAA922E127B0C70E22.description:
Explain how America’s founding, based on the words of the Declaration of Independence and the U.S.
Constitution, were unprecedented in human history.

498A7C34D1C94D76A841561412502465.description:
Analyze the Declaration of Independence and evaluate how the ideas expressed reflected the values and
principles of the founders' and influenced development of the United States, with an emphasis on
“inalienable rights” as inherent in all people by virtue of their being human meaning that they cannot be
surrendered to the government; the rights to “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness” being the
freedom to live, to protect rights, and to seek happiness as long as it does not violate the rights of
others; and the concept of “consent of the governed” and how this differed from rule under a monarch.

148C5EF5D2624297B6620A62C66AB046.description:
Explain the key reasons for the Patriots’ improbable victory and analyze major battles of the American
Revolution, including the Battle of Trenton, the Battle of Saratoga, and Yorktown.

5A10BFEA851C47CCAD96388CF4736785.description:
Explain the historical context of and the events leading to the signing of the Declaration of
Independence including the Boston Massacre, Boston Tea Party, Patrick Henry’s “Give Me Liberty or
Give Me Death” speech, the battles at Lexington and Concord and Bunker Hill, the Second Continental
Congress and failed Olive Branch Petition, and Thomas Paine’s Common Sense.

92BA77D412DD44C3978574B2F49D5F33.description:
Analyze the development of the United States from the American Revolution through the ratification of the
U.S. Constitution and Early Republic.

1A78E83A0B204DBF8FCECE623363158D.description: Compare and contrast content and viewpoints.

5841052C93964150B17B87CEDDE8BFFB.description: Demonstrate an understanding of social studies content.

A8F06A00F31346B1904BAE9C35EB12E4.description:
Construct and express claims that are supported with relevant evidence from primary and/or secondary
sources, social studies content knowledge, and clear reasoning and explanations to:

64B335178178495C87ACDA67B5B0EFC9.description: Explain how the availability of sources affects historical interpretations.

A3502643E94B4F648376BCAE83D1BAC4.description: Compare and contrast multiple sources and accounts.

6112ED3D62534522A0994E8BAD8DAE75.description: Use a variety of primary and secondary sources to:

AFEADE8973484B2DA2B0F5CA252A44CD.description:
Use geographic representations and demographic data to analyze environmental, cultural, economic and
political characteristics and changes.

BA2FF22E66A44C40AFB8EDB88BD6FB6E.description: Compare and contrast events and developments in U.S. history from 1776 to 2008.

D591CC144CF347FC9AE9B5C80F5C57DF.description:
Analyze connections between events and developments in U.S. history within their global context from
1776 to 2008.

CABBE3FA3A014F358CFB9C3DDF30B236.description:
Analyze ideas and events in the history of the United States of America from 1776 to 2008 and how they
progressed, changed, or remained the same over time.

document.title: 2022 K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Social Studies

23F406DBA1AF46DB967CBFEFED7C5D25.description:
Create a budget and explain its importance in achieving personal financial goals and avoiding negative
financial consequences.

EB2D1A3E911544B6BBAB6FB0903EC6C9.description:
Compare types of credit, savings, investment, and insurance services available to the consumer from
various institutions.

6891C50BF2684AE68A7DE1868BE1BFE0.description: Explain the benefits and risks of using credit and examine the various uses.

F7ADE58F0C794F0CA1E98AC776207D38.description:
Apply given financial data to real life situations such as balancing a checking account, reading bank and
credit card statements, purchasing major goods, and avoiding consumer fraud.

FA598165B5E14927878BF03E458E0879.description: Explain the relationship between education, training, and career options to future earning potential.

CDAFDEEFAB814299A7B3BFD185CD61AA.description:
Apply economic principles to make sound personal financial decisions, including in regards to income,
money management, spending and credit, and savings and investing.

63D639F68B94456B848B829B6044C2BB.description:
Explain the effects of specialization and trade on the production, distribution, and consumption of goods
and services for individuals, businesses, and societies.

4A1ABC19B1A44CF3A947007E2A60B362.description:
Explain ways in which competition, free enterprise, and government regulation influence what is
produced and allocated in an economy, including national and global consequences.

C214EE35C5E846B7BD959B7D56A14989.description:
Explain the factors that influence the production and distribution of goods by individuals and businesses
operating in a market system, including monopolistic competition, perfect competition, monopoly, and
oligopoly; credit; currencies; economic indicators; factors of production (land, labor, capital,
entrepreneurship); goods and services; price; roles of consumers and producers; rule of law; and supply
and demand.

4827FF6DD7F44438BC12D71448BB1604.description:
Analyze the role of government institutions in developing and implementing economic policies, and
explain the effects of government policies on market outcomes, including both intended and
unintended consequences.

95818B7FB5794C69BD1E773D85A7391D.description: Describe different perspectives on the role of government regulation in the economy.

3E214008F7874883B61A4E932FBBE017.description: Compare and contrast capitalism and socialism as economic systems.

FAB107D449AC40678159D97CBA5A4E91.description:
Explain ideas presented in Adam Smith's “The Wealth of Nations,” including his ideas about free markets
and the “invisible hand.”

7CF57412EC9E405DBB52D5043417F068.description:
Explain elements of the United States economy within a global context and economic principles required to
make sound financial decisions.

2B43A044391E4CBF95B8C21065824595.description: Describe the development of and challenges to international law after World War II and the Holocaust.

A935CD97CA3A49D489F1F184AF0F93FF.description:
Explain the origins and purpose of international organizations and agreements, including the United
Nations, NATO, NAFTA, and USMCA; and analyze how the United States and member nations work to
cooperate politically and economically.

2CB0486D8CB74A42B1021EC383122475.description:
Analyze interactions between the United States and other nations over time and effects of those
interactions.

F489C09CE46B4ECCB484F2CA49A06F15.description:
Analyze the development, implementation, and consequences of U.S. foreign and domestic policies over
time, including how U.S. policies are influenced by other countries and how they influence political
debates.

A5D99562A0374ED49F39F562A37EB2E6.description:
Distinguish between foreign and domestic policies, and analyze major U.S. foreign and domestic policies,
including those in education; health care; immigration; naturalization; regulation of business and
industry; foreign aid; and intervention abroad.

C0EC26A1A049426A8674A0129B3D503C.description: Analyze the issues of foreign and domestic policy of the United States.

6074E96313EC4832818FC14DDCE25A82.description: Describe local and parish governments in Louisiana, including police juries and home rule charters.

352662E0E90F4332B94FC2A60878883A.description:
Evaluate the processes for drawing Louisiana’s congressional districts and their effect on statewide and
national elections.

4C80F17BAACB44E7A2DA058B26D5F3DB.description:
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of technologies in politics and government and how they
affect media, civic discourse, and the credibility of sources.

6FD0A98BD84E4CB794DE44A59A6AA095.description:
Evaluate how the media affects politics and public opinion, including how public officials use the media
to communicate with the people.

34646F3353644F9C9CA0269E022442B7.description:
Analyze issues and challenges of the election process, including gerrymandering; at-large voting; voter
turnout; and voter access policies.

31E3C1B651E343E2BDD70515091EEC9E.description:
Evaluate the purpose, structure, and function of the Electoral College, including how it aims to ensure
representation for less populated states.

33C84C74306E4DA688EB07D403111AE6.description:
Explain rules governing campaign finance and spending and their effects on the outcomes of local, state,
and federal elections.

7D0550582C894CE783F541B9EF29D3A5.description:
Explain historical and contemporary roles of political parties, special interest groups, lobbies/lobbyists,
and associations in U.S. politics.

11F0E4B6ED13453990185530931EB4EE.description: Describe U.S. citizenship requirements and the naturalization process in the United States.

DB234CF6319E461E80B6AE7DB1F114FF.description:
Analyze the duties and responsibilities of citizens in the United States, including paying taxes, serving on
a jury, obeying the law, voting, and Selective Service registration.

D58CC7F12BC34878932EAA8388729F80.description: Analyze political processes and the role of public participation in the United States.

A216DC26747149E2B664213F0E40DDDD.description: Analyze political processes and the role of public participation in the United States.

6606307ED58B4FE3B77A67E204BB5CA2.description:
Describe equal protection and due process as defined by the U.S. Constitution, and explain how states
subverted equal protection during the Jim Crow era.

0EEE442B7CAA4EC6BFF041906BFE45BC.description: Analyze the rights enumerated in the Bill of Rights and their application to historical and current issues.

EA9B3556312B4101B264C10C8266D861.description: Explain how the U.S. Constitution protects individual liberties and rights.

F06CFB1F259B47B997E231B2455D0676.description:
Evaluate how civil rights and civil liberties in the United States have developed and been protected by the
U.S. government over time.

64AF2B42D5A64EF78D2120B32C1503E2.description:
Explain the historical connections between Civil Law, the Napoleonic Code, and Louisiana’s system of
laws.

FA29C8DF82E3477497106EAC881001CF.description:
Analyze continuity and change in the Louisiana State Constitution over time, and compare and contrast
the Louisiana State Constitutions and the U.S. Constitution.

13F1678E4BA04368B8821D5225F71FC3.description:
Analyze how federal, state, and local governments generate and allocate revenues to carry out the
functions of government.

D953E039361A4AC88B2A07C247B6EC0C.description:
Analyze how the Constitution has been interpreted and applied over time by the legislative, executive,
and judicial branches, including loose and strict constructionist interpretations.

06FBFAFDEAD0411CA4A04890BFBFE2F8.description:
Analyze the structure, powers, and functions of the judicial branch of the U.S. federal government,
including checks on the other branches of government; powers of the judicial branch such as those to
interpret laws and decide the constitutionality of laws; nomination and appointment process of federal
judges, origin of judicial review; and significance of stare decisis.

7E106198D6144A1C897C3BA89E39384D.description:
Analyze the structure, powers, and functions of the executive branch of the U.S. federal government,
including checks on other branches of government; powers of the executive branch such as those to
carry out and enforce laws, issue executive orders, and conduct diplomacy with other nations; duties of
the president, vice president, and Cabinet; presidential nominations, appointments, and confirmations;
and the concept of the “bully pulpit.”

C9FEF0F5AD984EABBEF7168FF4FD7549.description:
Analyze the structure, powers, and functions of the legislative branch of the U.S. federal government,
including rules of operations of Congress; checks on the other branches of government; powers of the legislative branch such as those to make laws, declare war, tax and spend; and duties of representatives,
senators, leadership (Speaker of the House, the Senate President Pro Tempore, majority and minority
leaders, party whips), committees, and commissions.

2C0863C78FBB4BD88CE1DC6A5DDCB82F.description:
Explain the structure and processes of the U.S. government as outlined in the U.S. Constitution,
including the branches of government; federalism; how a bill becomes a law at the federal level; and the
process for amending the U.S. Constitution.

FE9A8A0D95554CFCAC2173F8A802CFF6.description:
Compare and contrast the powers and responsibilities of local, state, tribal (including the Chitimacha
Tribe of Louisiana, the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana, the Jena Band of Choctaw Indians, and the TunicaBiloxi Indian Tribe), and federal governments, and explain how each is financed, how they interact with
each other, and how citizens interact with and within each of them.

9E92DFA12E574E5F93B3B1E50DE4EE16.description: Analyze the structure, roles, responsibilities, powers, and functions of governments in the United States.

FF984E22AF9A4D87B3DB525F14E25F8F.description:
Evaluate the fundamental principles and concepts of the U.S. government including Creator-endowed
unalienable rights of the people, due process, equal justice under the law, equal protection, federalism,
frequent and free elections in a representative government, individual responsibility, individual rights,
limited government, private property rights, popular sovereignty, right to privacy, rule of law, the
supremacy clause, and the separation of powers with checks and balances.

C07BACE314164B3FAFEC7EB8EE5A985B.description:
Explain how the concept of natural rights that precede politics or government influenced the foundation
and development of the United States.

E8F5BCF738EA4D79ABB670A1C328B965.description:
Analyze the issues related to various debates, compromises, and plans surrounding the drafting and
ratification of the 1789 Constitution of the United States.

5C37A80129AD481CA9CFA63258D63A01.description:
Analyze the foundational documents and ideas of the United States government and its formation,
including Magna Carta, the Mayflower Compact, Enlightenment philosophies, English Bill of Rights,
Declaration of Independence, the Articles of the Confederation, the Constitution of the United States of
America and the Bill of Rights, and the Federalist papers, and their role and importance in the origin and
development of the nation.

E9D9A80890D44076B72042A29D721F8A.description:
Explain historical and philosophical factors that influenced the government of the United States,
including Enlightenment philosophers such as Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, Charles de Montesquieu,
Jean-Jacques Rousseau, as well as the Great Awakening.

E02CCD04975C4A988DBB6F830D220FBE.description:
Compare different systems and structures of government, including constitutional republic and
autocracy, direct democracy and representative democracy, presidential system and parliamentary
system, unicameral and bicameral legislatures, and unitary, federal, and confederate systems.

B951F37F8C6948FB9F8245BB33D37231.description: Describe the purpose of government and competing ideas about the role of government in a society.

8C09E4DC6DF74DC4B4C0204436749A9E.description:
Analyze factors that influenced the Founding Fathers and the formation and development of the
government of the United States.

6280C05562C54E009DA62FF8191731F8.description: Compare and contrast content and viewpoints.

D86200345DE843B1AD00D99388625581.description: Demonstrate an understanding of social studies content.

2CBA8E005CF640C1AD09E3C003BE375C.description:
Construct and express claims that are supported with relevant evidence from primary and/or secondary
sources, social studies content knowledge, and clear reasoning and explanations to:

728E12F9E5A24F4CA1A0DCC7A3DCB4E3.description: Explain how the availability of sources affects historical interpretations.

F44A1AC8DFA64C2E9DC57FFC57645910.description: Compare and contrast multiple sources and accounts.

6FDA0D0D61DF4BA6AA6D4502A24A6B04.description: Use a variety of primary and secondary sources to:

6FFA778A3FB84BF192E7EE8989AEE3FA.description:
Use geographic representations, demographic data, and geospatial representations to analyze civic issues
and government processes

1FFE714C50A34A29AE9F60EA66B913EF.description:
Explain connections between ideas, events, and developments related to U.S. history and government, and
analyze recurring patterns, trends, and themes.

89310A71E41A4D9AA1CEF2B136BA1111.description: Compare and contrast events and developments in U.S. history and government.

C6228A6E449E4D7F835B01DFD1CD9C99.description:
Analyze causes and effects of events and developments in U.S. history, including those that influenced laws,
processes, and civic participation.

C5EFFE23C67F4E38BAD8AE1C06208C8C.description:
Evaluate continuity and change in U.S. government, politics, and civic issues throughout U.S. history,
including those related to the powers of government, interpretations of founding documents, voting trends,
citizenship, civil liberties, and civil rights.

document.title: K-12 Louisiana Student Standards for Mathematics

42F49A5934BD419FB5ECDF7632138E43.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

0BA9B7DA1D444D0C8D3FEADD50144F35.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret
the answer in terms of the model.

7CD8EBDD04884D08AA6A224BE808DBCD.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

DEC0E8B3DB3B4763B3307EC63AC17BC6.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and
everyday situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance
of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

518F0294AD444AB8A9E6C2E85F95BAF8.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object
being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to
approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your
school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for
other subjects and compare the results.

65653C05BD5E49B78AB08C2B53D6FC50.description:
Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as
saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional
probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

141E1B8DEFF04229B7AC24D6CEFC605E.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the
product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

BF69701682E746688D9F35D874E30ACE.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the
outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events (“or,” “and,” “not”).

D5BF691136BD4E0E8B99ABAB5D04E293.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

943B39F29C7141199E6D12375DC1F8AE.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

40AB0CDBAD3F4569A8B55FA84F9DA9F7.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical
constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios). ★

D67A6E702F1848AB9931BE7CE636A20E.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs
per cubic foot).★

758553C8CB3446968F440C50BC3BE945.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a
human torso as a cylinder).★

844010DC74564EB7A7DC0EEEE2FE7281.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

D6F0ABEF6AEE491E96CEF909DF9A0764.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

997AFF2595F449CF8ABAB5842D34DA42.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

255FBBE81C224A23BCD195132574BC21.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.★

35FCD7E6A0C0441EBC0F45E497D077C2.description:
Give an informal argument, e.g., dissection arguments, Cavalieri’s principle, or informal limit arguments, for the
formulas for the circumference of a circle; area of a circle; volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

744991F3EAB14C289B4B78920101AA2F.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

3293F1F1C9CF46CBA462BEB8FC283559.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the
distance formula.★

7F5AD2D17556409A912B82953F6E8371.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

2811C3612CA64F11B76423BD12C1717C.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find
the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

8EF6E4DDABE141F28CD7C33F18E1FF33.description:
Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or disprove that a figure
defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3 ) lies on
the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

78F81B769A0B47138AE1C16D8BE530A7.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

1869B905BE3347FF9689633454CF004D.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square
to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

7FA95E710A4847B2A96484B2A0AC24B3.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

B519CEEADB1A4849BD749B3785C6B835.description:
Use similarity to determine that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and
define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a
sector.

E6DC78083C4A44FBA5794912675A172F.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

B75A8C0B56D54EE08B7B444C22FE8E43.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral
inscribed in a circle.

CB0025549BD14951916B101980260929.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords, including the following: the
relationship that exists between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are
right angles; and a radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

1EBA9017E460487E8B68E8A377CB3498.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

89A98345ABC54DA5B0FD4D12948BA639.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

8F5D7AD6A29247EB92C49A994BABD832.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.★

151420AD5C554D03B07BC65519E5131E.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

1EAC3FFB4BD04960B5C125F24308247F.description:
Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles, including special right triangles (30-60-90 and 45-45-
90), are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

256194C9AD3C4E1BAEF3917F3A50B4E3.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

3A170B58E5264BAFB0FF328E7289BBFA.description:
Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric
figures.

433B0B38FCC645CA955350EAC1330924.description:
Prove and apply theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the
other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity; SAS
similarity criteria; SSS similarity criteria; AA similarity criteria

1B49918C896547889B1F390DF2D04674.description: Prove and apply theorems involving similarity.

F4D8241372E94A2CAA95311549614B23.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

70A3EB58EADD42B182F5CE9552656829.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are
similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all
corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

CC28057A15E44E61947F3E266FA99071.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

DA1A319870CF438E9DB62F543C7F16AB.description:
A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing
through the center unchanged.

15142A75A8BA44C5BBC93E215E02F631.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:

1B9FAECCB080472C8E24230457E36136.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

4A798224F7924B93B68C35532355CA29.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

8171376CE1984799A4E4494CDBAAB7B2.description:
Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods, e.g., compass and straightedge,
string, reflective devices, paper folding, or dynamic geometric software. Examples: copying a segment; copying
an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular
bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

282757088B6841DD91E60E02F56EA341.description:
Prove and apply theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite
angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are
parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

F4EA0B2BBC69438083AB842868583CBD.description:
Prove and apply theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to
180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is
parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

70FB9EDDE15A475F995E5B8EB4F79189.description:
Prove and apply theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a
transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are
congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment’s
endpoints.

5DA1999B4814409F8A0554A5A3999713.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in
terms of rigid motions.

FBA5C0EA2A2C405A951807B6796E81F7.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if
corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

49CB20341AB84667A2806377D93AE48E.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion
on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they
are congruent.

3B19DFC979224D6592A969B307726564.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

59A1D4E2549046138030AB5DE3BF69D7.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph
paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure
onto another.

FE1F905664CC4032B7E5E0EE3BB2A081.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines,
parallel lines, and line segments.

5A01C8643D7D43F1976661B6E9FFEA16.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry
it onto itself.

941A7234BBFF4DCE9EC250CE0CD0A9CD.description:
Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies, tracing paper, or geometry software;
describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs.
Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus
horizontal stretch).

0C444FEF7BF04459917C17CFACAD9758.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the
undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

D34DC163B04D49A183593989968890F4.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

4A8808522F674EAA9E8FA9BD26284925.description:
Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and/or other living things in
the local environment.

492A994C287A4324B67902961DE46A1B.description:
Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting to prepare for and respond to
severe weather.

EBEF2EE9CE6441549B1C4E31911A2535.description:
Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants or animals (including humans) and
the places they live.

6C1B2FE2E11B48609CC48A1EE7FAC52B.description:
Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the
environment to meet their needs.

BF8A3D7367ED4E1ABFB8C5453AA3AA9E.description: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.

D6B503BC64984FE691C632628C68C927.description: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.

A3DE5787AB0D408EB1135EB3FB6F30F2.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

CCFCB46242264B11827929E9FF4DE028.description: Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.

3DD35E557CB94C5ABE52A74EA0C94715.description: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth’s surface.

D1D9671E5B9D4339B50327CC49C98DB6.description:
Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with
a push or a pull.

C7AEA3C7E2CA4FF080D6E1AB0F090D19.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.

51BFF041134A4AC8B3CD9D6AE051FE1C.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

9B49BF1C826E442AAE3C596818D00E1E.description:
Evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning behind the idea that electromagnetic radiation can be described
either by a wave model or a particle model, and that for some situations one model is more useful than the other.

778240B38E964FE98124D34EBF505810.description:
Use mathematical representations to support a claim regarding relationships among the frequency, wavelength,
and speed of waves traveling in various media.

83DEDB79597A4546BC6F0AFFD2CA6771.description: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

699A91E6A715439DB746AC05DA80AABC.description:
Develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to illustrate the forces
between objects and the changes in energy of the objects due to the interaction.

7D0801680419421E856F848D53B6D204.description:
Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components
of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among
the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).

9A1BC8CBF1E54CE78121AB1A3CD099A8.description:
Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another
form of energy.

A345754336D84DA79777C8A968D2EAD8.description:
Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as a combination
of energy associated with the motions of particles (objects) and energy associated with the relative positions of
particles (objects)

A2B86E1607A34227823ABB3A5439A524.description:
Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the
change in energy of the other component(s) and energy flows in and out of the system are known.

BB50993B95D840CB93A68FFD68682EF2.description:
Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that an electric current can produce a magnetic field and
that a changing magnetic field can produce an electric current.

126A2FFC93CE40C0BEA7FD05655DA795.description:
Use mathematical representations of Newton’s Law of Gravitation and Coulomb’s Law to describe and predict the
gravitational and electrostatic forces between objects.

F99998AEA9C24D658B5B37F9AA36BE73.description:
Apply scientific and engineering ideas to design, evaluate, and refine a device that minimizes the force on a
macroscopic object during a collision.

344F4F1D2B374DD3BF48E147679F5210.description:
Use mathematical representations to support the claim that the total momentum of a system of objects is
conserved when there is no net force on the system.

9969F042BD1F46E6AB03DAF40C5A5DBB.description:
Analyze data to support the claim that Newton’s second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship
among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.

99A3D183C64B499BA87672EA316DB33A.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

B901256024F64F72AA328A9D819C2551.description:
Use a computational representation to illustrate the relationships among Earth systems and how those
relationships are being modified due to human activity.

0095476311E346AAABFA80E7F0C3BCA3.description:
Analyze geoscience data and the results from global climate models to make an evidence-based forecast of the
current rate of global or regional climate change and associated future impacts to Earth systems.

E4693E1FC6AB4BBE933E48FE6CC8E1F4.description: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.

2598283CCE8547979E2BB6E1EA5C0EE4.description:
Create a computational simulation to illustrate the relationships among management of natural resources, the
sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity

85FD3EEFD3BF46E290F1DD45C358E0C3.description:
Evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and utilizing energy and mineral resources based
on cost-benefit ratios.

D5F1B39DFE044192A1D8064F885783FC.description:
Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural
hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.

553F5C42C3EC48FDB793EB22219DD7A1.description:
Apply scientific reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planetary surfaces to
construct an account of Earth’s formation and early history.

645C0833FF844A9297126D4055EA9DE8.description:
Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant
galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.

9A665C6BC76F44E7A419DA35321AD4F3.description: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous coevolution of Earth systems and life on Earth.

4D1DEA6F051C4CCF9E3A1BAE98D0507B.description:
Develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere,
geosphere, and biosphere.

EDF1E3D4F73F4332AD1265925E974934.description: Plan and conduct an investigation on the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.

C39E8869F07244879C5AAD2340380E37.description:
Analyze and interpret data to explore how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth’s systems result in
changes in atmosphere and climate.

8F0C91A83CED4489958115218FEC31B8.description: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth’s interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.

8FD5C7C5BE754C1DAAF2EB4D91D1DC8F.description:
Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth’s surface can create feedbacks that cause
changes to other Earth’s systems.

71644CFE362145BA9FBA49C36ED8E6F5.description:
Develop a model to illustrate how Earth’s internal and surface processes operate at different spatial and temporal
scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.

D6B139F318804EDF88CEAB96A1344862.description:
Evaluate evidence of the past and current movements of continental and oceanic crust and the theory of plate
tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.

99F55DA97DEB41F09E79C1D80D20D794.description: Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.

68F91DA93EF949C998006A553500D070.description: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.

A5AB40FCEC424C5E82A23F2DE0FEB870.description:
Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the sun and the role of nuclear fusion in the sun’s
core to release energy that eventually reaches Earth in the form of radiation.

15FC76721348499C998A88FDCA47F307.description: Describe the geographic, political, economic, and cultural structures of Indigenous civilizations of the Americas.

57FAE856A14E47759AC24BA08974C8ED.description: Compare and contrast heliocentric and geocentric theories of the Greeks (geocentric) and Copernicus (heliocentric).

D75BDBD099AB4F05A6933678B7626036.description: Explain the significant causes of the Protestant Reformation, including the selling of indulgences and Martin Luther's 95 Theses.

1DDCC55B7E66469AAE4955294DDE92C9.description: Explain how Johannes Gutenberg's printing press affected the growth of literacy and diffusion of knowledge.

15A481FAE8D34EFA994BBAB11311B953.description: Explain the development of Renaissance art, including the significance of Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, William Shakespeare, and systems of patronage.

CC1CC9CC59C54CF3915359D67DB064BF.description: Identify the importance of Florence, Italy and the Medici Family in the early stages of the Renaissance.

C947161F599E4DB79EACE7F5F7ABDA97.description: Describe the role of the Trans-Saharan caravan trade in the changing religious and cultural characteristics of West Africa and in the exchange of salt, gold, and enslaved people.

ECDBCE0194DE447CB251FEE2D6B985B9.description: Describe the growth of the kingdoms of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai, including cities such as Djenne and Timbuktu as centers of trade, culture, and learning.

6ED2FFFF235A4BC1BC95505DBD346D33.description: Identify and locate the geographic features of West Africa, including the Atlantic Ocean, Niger River, Djenne, the Sahara, Gulf of Guinea, and Timbuktu.

1DD5F32F213F4E3FB085B291E428E7DE.description: Describe the geographic, political, economic, and cultural structures of Medieval West African Kingdoms.

B19F7CFC71954AE78E995C28879AAC5D.description: Summarize the contributions of Islamic scholars in the areas of art, medicine, science, and mathematics.

C95C6C7E983D4FAEB0E178D481A67CA7.description: Describe the economic and social effects of the spread of the Black Death (Bubonic Plague) from Central Asia to China, the Middle East, and Europe, and its effect on the global population.

B75D685CE2A14255B4B6DDB37A6AAA85.description: Describe the development of feudalism and manorialism and their role in the medieval European economy.
